availableCommands.name: threejs-postprocess-outline-invisible-mesh
availableCommands.description:
Fix for a faint, screen-anchored rectangle/silhouette artifact when using a
Three.js screen-space outline (pmndrs `postprocessing` NormalPass + edge
Effect, or OutlineEffect). Use when: (1) a thin outlined box/quad appears in a
fixed screen position regardless of what's behind it (wall, floor, sky),
(2) it sits near a transparent/opacity-0 helper such as a muzzle-flash quad,
billboard, or decal, (3) you switched from inverted-hull to post-process
outlines. Root cause: NormalPass renders geometry into the normal buffer
ignoring material opacity/transparent/depthWrite, so an "invisible" (opacity 0)
mesh still produces normal edges that the outline pass draws. Fix: toggle the
mesh's `.visible`, not its opacity.

availableCommands.name: pg-search-tsvector-dictionary-mismatch
availableCommands.description:
Fix silent zero-result `pg_search` queries when the tsvector column is populated
by a DB trigger using one dictionary (e.g. `'spanish'`) but the `pg_search_scope`
matches with a different dictionary (defaults to `'simple'`). Use when:
(1) `pg_search_scope` with `tsvector_column:` returns empty arrays despite the
column being populated, (2) raw inspection shows `searchable: "'mendoz':2A 'carl':1A"`
but `Model.search_by_query('Mendoza')` returns `[]`, (3) generated SQL contains
`to_tsquery('simple', 'X':*)` while the column was built with `to_tsvector('spanish', …)`,
(4) Postgres full-text-search works in DB console with the right dictionary but
fails from Rails. Root cause: tsvector tokens are dictionary-specific (Spanish
stemming reduces 'Mendoza' to 'mendoz'; simple keeps it as 'mendoza'). The
matching side of the query MUST use the same dictionary as the index side.

availableCommands.name: bun-monorepo-dev-env-file-loading
availableCommands.description:
Fix a server/app that crashes at boot with undefined env vars (e.g. a Zod
`loadConfig()` ZodError for DATABASE_URL / S3_* / API keys, or
`process.env.X` being undefined) when run via a per-app dev script in a
bun + Turbo (or any) monorepo that keeps a single root `.env`. Use when:
(1) `bun run --cwd apps/<x> dev` or `bun --filter <pkg> dev` throws on
missing env even though a root `.env` exists, (2) the same command works
when run from the repo root cwd, (3) `next dev` only sees env when started
from apps/web, (4) you assumed Bun/Next walk up to find `.env`. Root cause:
Bun and Next.js auto-load `.env` ONLY from the invocation cwd and do NOT
traverse up to the monorepo root. Fix: load the root env explicitly with
`--env-file=../../.env` in each app's dev script.

availableCommands.name: temporal-worker-workflowspath-tsx-watch
availableCommands.description:
Fix Temporal worker crashing with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat
'.../src/workflows/index.js'` when running under `tsx watch` (or `ts-node`)
in dev. Use when: (1) `Worker.create({ workflowsPath })` resolves to a
`.js` path that doesn't exist because the worker is running directly from
TypeScript source (no `tsc` build), (2) the worker entry uses
`path.resolve(__dirname, './workflows/index.js')` and works in production
(`node dist/index.js`) but blows up the moment you switch dev to
`tsx watch src/index.ts`, (3) the stack trace ends in
`WorkflowCodeBundler.makeEntrypointPath` /
`WorkflowCodeBundler.createBundle` inside
`@temporalio/worker/src/workflow/bundler.ts`, (4) you're adding a
`yarn dev` parallel runner and the worker is the only service that fails.
Root cause: Temporal worker's webpack-based workflow bundler does a
`statSync` on `workflowsPath` before bundling. When `__dirname` resolves
to `packages/worker/src/` (under tsx-watch), only `.ts` files exist there.
The hardcoded `.js` extension was assuming compiled output. Fix: try `.ts`
first, fall back to `.js` — Temporal's bundler accepts either, since it
bundles via webpack rather than going through Node's loader.

availableCommands.name: biome-exclude-files-from-sorting
availableCommands.description:
Disable sorting rules for specific files in biome (e.g., package.json). Use when:
(1) biome lints files for sorted keys/properties, (2) you want to exclude specific
files from sorting, (3) you tried adding linter rules but sorting still happens.
Root cause: biome's sorting rules live in assist.actions.source, not linter rules.
Solution: use overrides section targeting assist (not linter), with correct syntax
for includes (plural, not include).

availableCommands.name: journal-gap-is-not-downtime
availableCommands.description:
Reconstruct why a Linux host stopped, after the fact, when its own journal just
ends. Use when: (1) journalctl shows a gap or a log that stops mid-stream with no
shutdown sequence, and you are about to call that gap "downtime", (2) `last` shows
a `reboot` with no preceding `shutdown` and you need to know if it crashed, hung,
or lost power, (3) there is no kernel panic, no OOM, no MCE and every software
hypothesis has been excluded, (4) you need to date the exact moment a clustered
node (Proxmox/corosync, etcd, pacemaker) stopped answering, (5) you are citing
SMART Unsafe_Shutdown_Count as proof of a specific power-loss event, (6) a second
host appears to corroborate a simultaneous reboot, (7) TWO OR MORE hosts
stopped within seconds of each other and you are treating them as separate
faults, (8) you are quoting a drive's Power_On_Hours as the machine's age. Covers: proving a journal gap
is a logging failure rather than an outage, reading corosync "Failed to receive
the leave message" as a clean-vs-unclean discriminator, verifying a witness host
is not a guest of the failed hypervisor, buffered-telemetry tail loss as an
instant-stop fingerprint, and why power loss and a hard hardware freeze cannot be
told apart from logs alone.

availableCommands.name: seo-surface-diff-verification
availableCommands.description:
Prove that a redesign/refactor of a static or SSG website (Astro, Next.js,
Hugo, etc.) did not change its SEO surface. Use when: (1) a client or SEO
agency requires that visual/UI changes leave SEO optimizations untouched,
(2) you need hard evidence that titles, meta tags, canonicals, heading
text/hierarchy, image alt text, link hrefs/anchors, JSON-LD, and visible
copy are byte-identical before and after a change, (3) reviewing a
"presentational-only" PR and wanting to verify that claim mechanically.
Builds the site before and after, extracts the SEO-relevant surface from
the emitted HTML with a stdlib-only Python script, and diffs the two JSON
snapshots for equality.

availableCommands.name: tsdown-from-tsup-migration
availableCommands.description:
Migrate from tsup to tsdown (tsup's successor). Use when: (1) replacing tsup with
tsdown in a Node.js TypeScript project, (2) seeing MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON Node.js
warning when running tsdown builds, (3) `node dist/index.js` fails after migration
because output file extension changed, (4) EVAL or INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT rolldown
warnings appear during tsdown build, (5) seeing "splitting: false is unsupported" errors,
(6) post-migration runtime crash `TypeError: _pkg.default is not a constructor` when a
package that exports a class as default (e.g. `SchemaBuilder` from `@pothos/core`) is
inlined into the CJS bundle — rolldown resolves the ESM `import` condition and the
interop wrapper can't bind the default export when the CJS file uses
`Object.defineProperty` getters. Covers config file migration, output extension changes,
warning suppression, the .mts config trick to avoid full ESM migration, and the
ESM-default-class interop fix via `deps.neverBundle`.

availableCommands.name: vitest-css-raw-import-empty
availableCommands.description:
Fix `import css from './file.css?raw'` silently yielding an empty string under
Vitest, which makes tests that parse stylesheet contents pass on nothing. Use
when: (1) a test reads CSS with `?raw` and every assertion passes even though
the file clearly has content, (2) a regex/parse over imported CSS throws
"could not find <block>" or returns `{}` while the same code works with
`node:fs`, (3) `console.log(String(cssSource).length)` prints `0` inside a
Vitest test, (4) you are asserting design-token values, CSS custom properties,
or theme contrast by reading a `.css` file in a test. Root cause: Vitest's
default `test.css: false` replaces CSS imports with empty stubs, and the stub
intercepts the `?raw` query too — it is NOT bypassed by `?raw`. Fix: set
`test.css: true` in vitest config. Dangerous because it fails green, not red.

availableCommands.name: backstage-app-packagename-breaks-backend-startup
availableCommands.description:
Backstage backend dies at startup with "Cannot find module 'app/package.json'"
when the frontend workspace is not literally named `app`. Use when: (1) the
backend logs `Plugin 'app' startup failed; caused by Error: Cannot find
module 'app/package.json'` and every plugin then behaves as if its data were
missing (empty catalog, empty search), (2) you named the frontend package
something other than `app` (`dev-app`, `portal`, `web`), (3) you are
hand-building a Backstage app inside an existing plugin monorepo rather than
using create-app. Root cause: `@backstage/plugin-app-backend` resolves the
frontend bundle by package name from `app.packageName`, defaulting to `app`,
and the frontend must also be a runtime dependency of the backend package.
The error names neither the config key nor the frontend package.

availableCommands.name: git-stash-pop-takes-foreign-stash
availableCommands.description:
Recover a stash that `git stash pop` silently consumed from ANOTHER branch,
and stop scripted stash/pop pairs from doing it. Use when: (1) a
`git stash push … && <do something> && git stash pop` sequence ends with
unexpected files modified in your working tree — files your task never
touched, (2) `git stash list` is one entry shorter than it was and the missing
entry belonged to a different branch, (3) you scripted "stash my changes, test
a clean tree, restore" and the tree was ALREADY clean, (4) you popped
something described `On <other-branch>: <message>`, (5) you need to un-drop a
stash. Root cause: `git stash push` on a clean tree is a NO-OP that creates
nothing and exits 0, so the paired `pop` takes whatever is now at `stash@{0}`
— the top of someone else's stack. Recovery via `git fsck --unreachable` and
`git stash store`.

availableCommands.name: tailwind-v4-removed-opacity-utilities
availableCommands.description:
Detect and fix silently dead bg-opacity-*/text-opacity-*/border-opacity-*
classes left behind after a Tailwind CSS v3 → v4 migration. Use when:
(1) an overlay, scrim, or tint looks washed out / missing after upgrading
to Tailwind 4 (e.g. hero text with poor contrast over a photo), (2) a
class like "hero-overlay bg-opacity-60" or "bg-black bg-opacity-50" has
no visible effect, (3) auditing a codebase post-migration. Tailwind v4
removed the *-opacity-* utilities (deprecated in v3) in favor of slash
syntax (bg-black/60) — leftover classes generate no CSS and fail
silently, so layouts look "almost right" and nobody notices.

availableCommands.name: gitlab-ci-duplicate-pipeline-at-mr-creation
availableCommands.description:
Fix GitLab CI running two pipelines for the same commit when a merge request is
opened. Use when: (1) opening an MR shows both a `push`/branch pipeline and a
`merge_request_event` pipeline on the identical SHA, seconds apart, (2) the
`.gitlab-ci.yml` already has GitLab's documented dedup rule
`if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH && $CI_OPEN_MERGE_REQUESTS / when: never` and it still
duplicates, (3) pipeline minutes / runner load doubled per MR, (4) a job gated on
`CI_MERGE_REQUEST_LABELS` (deploy-label gating) never fires on one of the two
pipelines. Root cause: `$CI_OPEN_MERGE_REQUESTS` is evaluated at pipeline-creation
time, so on the FIRST push the MR does not exist yet and the branch rule matches.

availableCommands.name: zot-registry-docker-deployment
availableCommands.description:
Deploy the Zot OCI container registry (project-zot/zot) with Docker or Docker
Compose. Use when: (1) writing a docker-compose.yml or Kubernetes manifest for
`ghcr.io/project-zot/zot`, (2) Zot logins fail for every user despite a
correct-looking htpasswd file, (3) new users added to htpasswd are never seen
by a running Zot, (4) a Zot `healthcheck:` marks the container permanently
unhealthy, (5) anonymous/unauthenticated clients can pull when they should not
(or you need to know which key controls that), (6) digest-pinned pulls
(`repo@sha256:...`) or signatures break through a Zot Docker Hub mirror,
(7) you are looking for `ZOT_*` environment variables and cannot find any.
Covers config-file-only configuration, bcrypt-only htpasswd, fsnotify reload,
accessControl policy semantics, distroless health endpoints, and sync setup.

availableCommands.name: better-auth-nextjs-signout-cookie-propagation
availableCommands.description:
Fix Better Auth server-side `auth.api.signOut()` (and other `auth.api.*` mutations)
silently failing to clear the session cookie in Next.js App Router. Use when:
(1) logout appears to succeed but user remains authenticated on next request,
(2) after `router.push("/login")` the user is immediately redirected back to the
protected area, (3) `useSession()` keeps returning a valid session for up to
`cookieCache.maxAge` (default 5 min) after signOut, (4) any `auth.api.*` call
from a custom Next.js route handler or server action needs to set/clear cookies
and they're not reaching the browser. Root cause: `auth.api.*` server methods
rely on the Better Auth response's `Set-Cookie` headers, which are NOT
auto-propagated to the Next.js response unless the `nextCookies()` plugin is
configured as the LAST plugin in the Better Auth config. Without it, the
headers are dropped when you return your own `NextResponse.json(...)`.

availableCommands.name: compose-env-empty-string-vs-unset
availableCommands.description:
Docker Compose's `KEY=${VAR:-}` always injects an EMPTY STRING into the container,
never an absent key — so apps that distinguish "unset" from "set but empty" fail to
start. Use when: (1) a container exits at startup with "<setting> must be non-empty",
"must not be blank", "cannot be empty", or a validation error naming a variable you
deliberately left blank, (2) an optional secret/credential breaks the app even though
the feature that needs it is disabled, (3) you copied .env.sample to .env and the
stack dies, while the same image runs fine with plain `docker run` and no -e flags,
(4) you want an optional env var that disappears entirely when unconfigured. Fix is
Compose's valueless `- VAR` form (key only, no equals sign). Covers the interaction
with --env-file/.env, and why ${VAR-} (single dash) does NOT help.

availableCommands.name: edge-guard-bypassed-by-path-encoded-param
availableCommands.description:
A proxy-level guard on a query parameter (nginx `$arg_<name>`, Traefik Query
matcher, a WAF rule) silently fails to protect an app whose router also
accepts that parameter encoded in the URL PATH. Use when: (1) you are adding
or reviewing an nginx `if ($arg_x ~ ...) { return 429; }` style rule in front
of a legacy CMS (Joomla/sh404SEF, Mambo, WordPress pretty permalinks, Drupal
path aliases, any SEF/"search engine friendly" router), (2) an expensive query
keeps reaching the database after such a guard was deployed and verified,
(3) slow-query logs show a request-controlled parameter (a deep `LIMIT`
OFFSET, a huge page size, an unfiltered id) whose name does NOT appear in the
matching access-log lines, (4) someone concludes "the guard works, so
pagination/param X is not involved" because the access log has no `?x=`,
(5) you are about to add a second edge rule for a newly observed encoding.
Root cause: nginx `$arg_*` reads ONLY the query string, while the app's
router rewrites path segments into `$_GET`/`$_REQUEST` before the handler
runs — so edge and app parse the URL under different grammars. Fix: bound the
value at application intake, after the rewriter has normalized every encoding.

availableCommands.name: ruby34-or-assign-block-syntax
availableCommands.description:
Ruby 3.4 raises SyntaxError for `||=` (or-assign) inside a brace block `{ }` when the
block is followed by trailing keyword arguments. Use when: (1) before_validation/before_create
with a block + `on:` option raises "unexpected write target", (2) migrating code from Ruby 3.3
to 3.4 that used `||=` inside `{ }` callbacks with keyword args, (3) any method call with
`method { obj.attr ||= value }, keyword: val` raises SyntaxError. Fix: extract to a named
method, or switch to do...end block with the keyword argument before the block.

availableCommands.name: tanstack-router-link-mock-href
availableCommands.description:
TanStack Router's Link component uses a `to` prop instead of `href`. When mocked
for React Testing Library tests, spreading `...props` onto an <a> element puts `to`
as a non-standard attribute — jsdom only gives role="link" to <a> elements with a
non-empty `href`. Use when: (1) `screen.getByRole('link')` or `getAllByRole('link')`
returns "Unable to find an accessible element with role link" in a test that renders
a TanStack Router Link, (2) the Link mock uses `{ children, ...props }` spread onto
an <a>, (3) tests pass locally but fail in CI with the same error.

availableCommands.name: tsx-watch-dev-server-process-port-cleanup
availableCommands.description:
Reliably stop/restart `tsx watch` (and Next.js) monorepo dev servers without
leaking duplicates or being misled about which process owns a port. Use when:
(1) `pkill -f 'packages/<x>/src/index.ts'` does NOT kill the dev server and
restarts keep spawning duplicates (multiple workers polling the same queue,
or "port already in use"/EADDRINUSE on restart), (2) `lsof -ti :PORT` reports
a PID that won't die or is actually a browser tab / another client, (3) you
can't tell which of several identical `tsx watch ... src/index.ts` processes
is the gateway vs the worker, (4) after several restarts you see 3-4 copies of
the same service. Root causes: tsx's command line is `tsx watch ... src/index.ts`
with a RELATIVE entry path (no package dir in it, so `-f 'pkg/src/index.ts'`
never matches), and `lsof -ti :PORT` matches CLIENT connections to the port
(e.g. Chrome, or a dev server connecting to the API) not just the LISTENER.

availableCommands.name: macos-realpath-symmetry-path-validation
availableCommands.description:
Fix false rejections in "path X must be inside directory Y" security checks
on macOS caused by asymmetric realpath. Use when: (1) a path-containment
check works on Linux/CI but rejects legitimate paths on macOS, (2) a test
using `mkdtempSync(tmpdir() + '/...')` triggers an error like "resolves to
/private/var/folders/... outside ~/...", (3) you've written a symlink-
hardening check that calls `realpathSync` on the file but not the parent
directory, (4) any code comparing `fs.realpathSync(filePath)` against a
user-config directory (HOME-derived, XDG-derived, or env-var-derived) with
`startsWith` or `===`. Root cause: macOS `os.tmpdir()` returns
`/var/folders/...` which is itself a symlink to `/private/var/folders/...`;
`realpathSync` resolves the file side to the `/private/...` form while the
unresolved directory side stays `/var/...`, so the prefix check fails. The
same trap fires for any user path whose prefix contains a symlink (custom
`~/.config` symlinked elsewhere, encrypted home dirs, etc.). Fix: realpath
BOTH sides before comparing, with a try/catch fallback for the case where
the directory doesn't exist yet on disk.

availableCommands.name: nodejs-scrypt-maxmem-limit-exceeded
availableCommands.description:
Fix Node.js/Bun `crypto.scrypt` throwing a memory-limit error with high
work factors. Use when: (1) hashing/verifying passwords throws
`Error: Invalid scrypt params` / `ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_SCRYPT_PARAMS`, or under
Bun `error:...:OPENSSL_internal:MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` /
`digital envelope routines::memory limit exceeded`, (2) a password login route
500s on every attempt while the params look fine, (3) you call `scrypt`/
`scryptSync` with `N` (cost) of 2^15+ (e.g. N=32768/65536/131072) and r=8,
(4) it works with small N in a quick test but fails with production params.
Root cause: scrypt needs ~128*N*r bytes (≈64 MiB at N=65536,r=8) but Node/Bun
default `maxmem` to 32 MiB. Fix: pass an explicit `maxmem` derived from the
params; raise maxmem, do NOT lower N (keep the OWASP-aligned work factor).

availableCommands.name: seed-fabricates-fields-ingest-never-writes
availableCommands.description:
Detect and fix the bug class where a dev seed/fixture script populates DB
columns the real ingest/write path never populates, so dashboards and
aggregate queries look correct locally and are permanently empty or wrong in
production. Use when: (1) a metric, panel, or column renders plausible
numbers on seeded data but reads `0`, `—`, or "no activity" against real
data, (2) a query filters on an enum/category literal (`WHERE kind = 'agent'`)
that no producer in the codebase can actually emit, (3) a comment or design
doc asserts "the client emits X" but grepping the client shows it only ever
emits Y, (4) a feature "worked when written" and nobody can say when it
broke, (5) you are reviewing any query whose WHERE clause compares a column
to a hardcoded string. Root cause: the seed was written to make dashboards
look right, so it back-fills fields the write path never produces; every
query built against seed data then passes review. Fix: assert filter literals
are a subset of producer-emittable values, with an anti-vacuity guard, and
make the seed call the same production code path.

availableCommands.name: git-worktrees-with-submodules
availableCommands.description:
Handle the full lifecycle of git worktrees that contain submodules: correct
removal AND recovery when removal left stale per-worktree config behind.
Use when: (1) `git worktree remove <path>` fails with
`fatal: working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed`,
(2) AFTER a child worktree was removed (or auto-cleaned by an agent runtime),
every `git` command in the main worktree fails with
`fatal: cannot chdir to '<deleted-path>/vendor/<sub>': No such file or directory`
and `fatal: '<op>' failed in submodule <path>`,
(3) `git worktree prune` does NOT fix the chdir error,
(4) `git -c submodule.recurse=false ...` works around it for single commands
but the corruption persists,
(5) you're cleaning up Claude Code background-agent worktrees under
`.claude/worktrees/agent-*/` for a repo with submodules,
(6) you also need to rebase local main after a squash-merge PR on GitLab/GitHub.
Root cause for the chdir error: the submodule's per-worktree `[core] worktree`
config line in `.git/modules/<sub>/config` and the
`.git/modules/<sub>/worktrees/<name>/` directory both survive worktree removal,
and `git worktree prune` does not touch them.
(7) inside a worktree where a registered submodule path was replaced with a
SYMLINK (a bootstrap shortcut to share the parent's checkout), `git status` /
`git commit` / `git rebase --continue` fail with `error: expected submodule
path '<path>' not to be a symbolic link` — and `-c submodule.recurse=false`
does NOT suppress it (see Part C).

availableCommands.name: changesets-action-worktree-version-leak
availableCommands.description:
`changesets/action` runs `changeset version` IN THE CHECKOUT to build its version PR,
leaving bumped package.json files in the working tree. Any later step in the same job
that reads `package.json` from disk sees the PROPOSED version, not the committed one —
so it tags, releases, or deploys a version that was never published. Use when:
(1) a git tag or GitHub release exists for a version absent from the registry,
(2) a release tag points at a feature-merge commit instead of the "chore: version
packages" commit, (3) a release workflow step reads `$(jq -r .version package.json)`
after a changesets step, (4) `npm view <pkg> versions` disagrees with `git tag -l`,
(5) a "release" job logs "creating pull request" with no publish line yet still
creates a tag. Fix: read versions from the commit — `git show "$GITHUB_SHA:path/package.json"`.

availableCommands.name: riot-lifecycle-state-timing
availableCommands.description:
Fix Riot.js components that render stale data one update behind, or whose
post-`update()` guard runs against the wrong value. Use when: (1) a derived
value assigned in `onUpdated` only appears after some later unrelated
re-render, (2) code reads `this.state.x` immediately after
`this.update({ x })` and gets the "wrong" (already-new) value, (3) a
conditional class / icon / disabled flag lags one render behind its prop,
(4) a DOM-only property such as `input.indeterminate`, `video.muted`,
`input.value` or `select.selectedIndex` never takes effect, (5) a child
component never re-renders when an async observable/event fires. Root cause:
`update()` merges state SYNCHRONOUSLY before re-rendering, and `onUpdated`
fires AFTER the DOM is written. Derive state in `onBeforeUpdate`, touch the
DOM in `onUpdated`.

availableCommands.name: mdast-to-string-welds-blocks-together
availableCommands.description:
`mdast-util-to-string` concatenates block nodes with no separator, so
stripping markdown with it produces "ChunkingApplied at index timeKeyDefault"
— words from adjacent blocks welded into tokens that match no search query.
Use when: (1) you need plain text from markdown for a search index, a
snippet, an excerpt, or an embedding, (2) stripped output has missing spaces
at paragraph, heading, list-item or table-cell boundaries, (3) full-text
search stops matching terms that are visibly present in the source, (4) you
reached for `toString(tree)` on a whole document rather than on a single
heading. Fix: walk the tree and treat paragraph/heading/tableCell/code as
units, joining them yourself.

availableCommands.name: tailwindcss-v4-monorepo-source-scanning
availableCommands.description:
Fix silent CSS class missing in TailwindCSS v4 monorepos after extracting components
to a shared workspace package. Use when: (1) layout regressions appear after moving
components to a shared package, (2) complex variant classes like data-[orientation=*],
group-data-[variant=*], or data-[state=active] appear in DOM but have no effect,
(3) basic utility classes (flex, text-sm, gap-2) work but data-attribute variants don't,
(4) build passes with no errors but CSS bundle is smaller than expected,
(5) getComputedStyle shows unexpected values despite correct class names in elements,
(6) an @source directive IS present and looks correct but the classes are still missing --
a @source pointing at a non-existent or gitignored path matches zero files SILENTLY,
which is indistinguishable from having no directive at all,
(7) one app in a monorepo renders shared-package styles correctly while a sibling app
does not, despite both appearing to declare @source.
Covers @tailwindcss/vite plugin, @tailwindcss/postcss, and workspace:* dependencies,
and the Next.js App Router relative-depth trap (src/app/globals.css vs src/index.css).

availableCommands.name: rails-locale-agnostic-error-tests
availableCommands.description:
Fix Rails model validation tests that fail when the app's primary I18n locale isn't English.
Use when: (1) `assert_includes model.errors[:field], 'is not included in the list'` fails
with `Expected ["no está incluido en la lista"] to include "is not included in the list"`
(Spanish) or similar in any other language, (2) `assert_equal "can't be blank", record.errors[:name].first`
fails because the message is localized, (3) test passes locally but fails in CI (or vice versa)
because the two environments have different default locales, (4) any test asserting against
literal Rails validation error text in a non-en-primary Rails app. Root cause: `errors[:field]`
returns I18n-translated strings; asserting against the English text assumes `I18n.default_locale = :en`.
Fix: assert against Rails' symbol-based error-details API which is locale-independent.

availableCommands.name: prisma-7-decimal-import-path
availableCommands.description:
Fix "Cannot find module '.../prisma-client/runtime/library'" or
"Cannot find module '@prisma/client/runtime/library'" TypeScript errors
after upgrading to Prisma 7. Use when: (1) TS2307 error on a `Decimal`
import that worked in Prisma 5/6, (2) import path is
`@prisma/client/runtime/library` or `<generated>/prisma-client/runtime/library`,
(3) upgrading from Prisma 5/6 to 7 and code does `import { Decimal } from ...`.
Root cause: Prisma 7 removed the `runtime/library` subpath from both the
`@prisma/client` package exports AND generated client output. `Decimal`
is now exposed only via the `Prisma` namespace as `Prisma.Decimal`.

availableCommands.name: agent-cli-nontty-stdin-hang
availableCommands.description:
Fix a headless AI-agent CLI (codex exec, pi, gemini, opencode, crush, aider,
claude -p) that hangs forever with no output when invoked from a script,
subprocess, CI job, MCP server, or background launcher. Use when: (1) stderr
shows "Reading additional input from stdin..." and nothing else ever happens,
(2) the process sits at 0% CPU with empty stdout and never exits, (3) the same
command works fine when you type it in a terminal but deadlocks under
automation, (4) a subprocess spawned with stdio:"pipe" never returns, (5) an
agent CLI "works interactively but not in my wrapper script". Root cause is
NOT the model, auth, or the network: the CLI detects a non-TTY stdin and blocks
waiting for an EOF that the parent never sends, even when the prompt was
already passed as a command-line argument. Fix is redirecting </dev/null.

availableCommands.name: verify-integration-contract-against-shipped-artifact
availableCommands.description:
Settle "does this tool's hook/event/webhook payload contain field X?" from the
vendor's SHIPPED ARTIFACT on disk rather than its documentation. Use when:
(1) you are about to build an integration on a payload field the docs do not
mention, or skip one because the docs omit it, (2) docs and observed behaviour
disagree, (3) you need to know whether a field is required or optional and the
docs only give an example, (4) you are deciding whether data is reachable at
all before committing to a capture mechanism, (5) a prior investigation closed
as "not available" and you are re-opening it, (6) a vendor changed pricing or
billing and you are unsure which docs pages are now stale. Root cause: docs
describe intent and lag releases; the installed binary, its bundled JSON
Schema, or its type definitions ARE the contract the tool enforces today.
Covers locating the artifact, extracting schemas from a compiled binary,
reading a shipped *.schema.json, and checking real state directories for files
the docs or third parties claim exist.

availableCommands.name: tailwindcss-v4-chart-colors
availableCommands.description:
Fix for invisible chart lines/bars in Recharts (or any SVG chart library) when using
TailwindCSS v4. Use when: (1) Chart lines/bars don't appear despite data existing,
(2) getComputedStyle returns stroke: "none" or fill: "none", (3) Project uses
TailwindCSS v4 with shadcn/ui, (4) Code uses hsl(var(--primary)) or hsl(var(--chart-1))
as SVG stroke/fill colors. Root cause: TailwindCSS v4 changed CSS custom properties
from HSL channel values to full OKLCH values — wrapping them in hsl() produces invalid
CSS and browsers silently fall back to "none".

availableCommands.name: biome-tailwind-v4-css-exclusion
availableCommands.description:
Fix Biome CSS parse errors caused by Tailwind v4 syntax (`@theme inline`,
`@import "tailwindcss"`). Use when: (1) `biome check` fails with "parse error"
on globals.css or similar file, (2) error points to `@theme inline { ... }` or
`@import "tailwindcss"` syntax, (3) Biome version 2.x, Tailwind v4+. Root cause:
Biome's built-in CSS parser does not support Tailwind v4 at-rule extensions.
Solution: exclude CSS files from Biome via `files.includes` in biome.json
(NOT `files.ignore` which is not a valid key in Biome 2.x).

availableCommands.name: prettier-html-parser-breaks-riot-templates
availableCommands.description:
Prettier's `html` parser silently corrupts Riot.js `.riot` templates and
breaks the build. Use when: (1) `npm run format` / a `prettier --parser html`
pass over `.riot` files is followed by a build failing with
"SyntaxError: Unexpected token, expected \",\"" from `@babel/parser` or
"(plugin at position N)" in rollup, (2) a diff shows `onclick="{ handler }"`
rewritten into a multi-line `onclick="\n  {\n    handler;\n  }\n"` block,
(3) `prettier -c` reports many `.riot` files as unformatted but running
`prettier -w` on them destroys the app, (4) deciding whether to add a
format-riot script to a Riot project. Root cause: Prettier treats every
`on*` attribute as JavaScript, but in Riot the braces are expression
delimiters, not a JS block. No riot-aware Prettier plugin exists on npm.
Fix: exclude `.riot` from Prettier entirely.

availableCommands.name: ai-agent-confirmation-gated-writes
availableCommands.description:
Architecture pattern for adding write capabilities to an AI tool-use agent while
keeping the agent loop entirely read-only. Use when: (1) you want an AI assistant
to be able to create records (tickets, work orders, part requests) without the model
having direct DB write access, (2) you need a user confirmation step before the write
fires, (3) the write should be attributed to the human user (not the AI) in the audit
trail, (4) you are exposing writes to an EXTERNAL autonomous agent (e.g. a remote MCP
server) where the agent itself confirms — see the threat-model variant: confirmation
does NOT constrain a self-confirming agent, so mutations with weak authorization
relative to their real-world effect (outbound SMS/email, token rotation) must be
denied at the exposure boundary. The "propose + sentinel + client-side mutation" pattern.

availableCommands.name: yarn-plugin-package-missing-peer-dep
availableCommands.description:
Fix Vite/rolldown/webpack production builds that fail with "failed to resolve import
'<X>/index.js' from '<Y>/index.js'" when `<Y>` is a plugin/extension package and `<X>`
is its required core/host package. Use when: (1) `yarn build` (or any production
bundler step) errors with `Rolldown failed to resolve import "@fullcalendar/core/index.js"
from "@fullcalendar/timegrid/index.js"` (or analogous: `@apollo/client` ↔
`@apollo/client-react`, `chart.js` ↔ `chartjs-plugin-*`, `recharts` ↔
`recharts-*` plugin packages, etc.), (2) dev server works but production build fails,
(3) typecheck passes but bundling fails (TypeScript reads peers via tsconfig
`moduleResolution`, but rolldown actually traverses the import graph), (4) you added
a plugin package (e.g. `@fullcalendar/timegrid`) without adding its peer host
(`@fullcalendar/core`). Root cause: Yarn 4 with `nodeLinker: node-modules` does NOT
auto-install peerDependencies — they must be declared in YOUR project's package.json.
Plugin packages declare `peerDependencies: { '@host/core': '~X.Y.Z' }` expecting
the consumer to install the host directly.

availableCommands.name: vitest-mock-once-queue-leak
availableCommands.description:
Fix confusing cross-test failures in Vitest caused by unconsumed mockResolvedValueOnce/
mockReturnValueOnce queue entries leaking into subsequent tests. Use when: (1) a test
fails asserting the wrong status code or return value but the mock setup looks correct,
(2) vi.clearAllMocks() in beforeEach doesn't fix the problem, (3) tests pass in
isolation but fail when the full suite runs, (4) a "once" mock was set in a test where
the mocked function was never actually called (because an earlier step in the handler
threw or returned early). Symptoms look like mock bleed-through between tests.

availableCommands.name: git-clone-into-mktempdir
availableCommands.description:
Fix for "destination path already exists and is not an empty directory" when using
git clone with a mkdtemp/mkdtempSync temporary directory as the target. Use when:
(1) implementing git clone into a temp dir, (2) clone fails silently or with ENOENT,
(3) using simple-git, child_process, or any git wrapper with mkdtempSync/mkdtemp.
Root cause: mkdtempSync creates the directory before clone runs; git clone requires
target to be absent or empty. Fix: clone into a subdirectory of the temp dir.

availableCommands.name: android-vpn-swallows-inbound-lan-server-replies
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose an Android-hosted server (Termux sshd, HTTP server, Syncthing) that is
unreachable from the LAN while an Android VPN (Tailscale, WireGuard, Clash,
AdGuard, V2Ray) is active or set as Always-on. Use when: (1) `ssh` fails with
"Connection timed out during banner exchange", (2) nmap reports the port `open`
but no banner/data ever arrives and the connection just hangs, (3) the same
server answers instantly when tested FROM the phone against its own LAN IP,
(4) a port shows `filtered`/timeout while other closed ports return
ECONNREFUSED, (5) `ss` in Termux fails with a permission error. Two known
causes: (a) the phone routes LAN-destined traffic into the VPN tunnel — often
because a tailnet peer advertises a subnet route covering the LAN — so the
app's replies leave via the tun instead of wlan0; (b) Android 17+ Local
Network Protection blocks apps from accepting inbound LAN connections by
default. Fix: connect over the VPN's own IP (works for both), or disable
Always-on VPN / stop accepting the LAN subnet route / grant the local
network permission.

availableCommands.name: threejs-outline-grazing-angle-black-surfaces
availableCommands.description:
Fix screen-space outline / edge-detection post effects (NormalPass + depth
edge shader, postprocessing lib, custom cel outlines) painting ENTIRE flat
surfaces solid outline-color. Use when: (1) crate tops, floors toward the
horizon, walls at glancing angles, or geometry very close to the camera
render as giant black slabs/blobs while front-facing surfaces look fine,
(2) the artifact moves/changes with the camera angle, (3) textures load fine
and materials are correct so it looks like a lighting/shadow bug but isn't.
Root cause: a relative depth-edge threshold fires across whole surfaces at
grazing view angles. Fix: scale the depth delta by the view-space normal's
|n.z| (slope compensation) with a small floor.

availableCommands.name: actioncable-single-use-ticket-auth
availableCommands.description:
Authenticate an ActionCable WebSocket with a short-lived, single-use ticket
instead of a long-lived JWT/token in the connection URL, WITHOUT breaking
auto-reconnect. Use when: (1) security review flags "secrets/JWT in URL" for a
`/cable?token=<jwt>` handshake, (2) you must replace a URL-borne credential
with a one-time ticket but the consumer is long-lived and auto-reconnects,
(3) a naive "fetch ticket then createConsumer(url)" works on first connect but
the socket dies permanently after the ticket's TTL because reconnects reuse
the consumed/expired ticket. Covers the Redis-backed single-use ticket store
(atomic GET+DEL) and the reconnect-safe synchronous URL-function pattern for
@rails/actioncable.

availableCommands.name: pothos-prisma-7-generator-setup
availableCommands.description:
Configure @pothos/plugin-prisma with Prisma 7 correctly. Use when:
(1) Setting up Pothos + plugin-prisma for the first time in a Prisma 7
project, (2) Pothos builder errors with "dmmf is required" or similar,
(3) The generated pothos-prisma-types file contains an absolute
filesystem path in its import (e.g.
`/Users/.../src/generated/prisma-client/index.js`) that breaks CI or
other machines, (4) Migrating away from typegraphql-prisma.
Root cause: Prisma 7 no longer exposes DMMF on client internals, so
plugin-prisma ≥ 4.13 requires explicit `dmmf: getDatamodel()` from the
generator-produced types file; and the generator needs a `clientOutput`
option to emit a relative import instead of an absolute path.

availableCommands.name: graphql-codegen-enums-as-types
availableCommands.description:
Fix TypeScript error TS1294 "This syntax is not allowed when 'erasableSyntaxOnly' is enabled"
caused by graphql-codegen generating 'export enum' declarations. Use when: (1) tsc fails with
TS1294 on generated graphql.ts file, (2) project uses TypeScript erasableSyntaxOnly or
verbatimModuleSyntax, (3) you want enum types as string union types instead of TypeScript enums
so they work with 'export type' re-exports. Add enumsAsTypes: true to codegen config.
Also covers converting a manual enums.ts barrel to auto-generated re-exports.

availableCommands.name: sec-13f-value-dollars-not-thousands
availableCommands.description:
Fix 13F institutional-holdings values being 1000x too large, and three related
EDGAR parsing traps. Use when: (1) parsing a Form 13F `informationTable` XML
and multiplying `<value>` by 1000 "because SEC reports in thousands",
(2) a 13F-derived portfolio total is implausibly huge (a filer's book coming
out in the trillions), (3) implied price-per-share from `<value>/<sshPrnamt>`
is absurd (e.g. $289,000/share for Apple), (4) an EDGAR "current filings" Atom
feed parser matches zero entries, (5) fetching `primary_doc.xml` or a
`*table*.xml` from an EDGAR filing returns 404, (6) a `type=4` feed query
returns 424B2/424B3/425/485BPOS filings. Root cause for (1)-(3): SEC changed
`<value>` from thousands to WHOLE DOLLARS in EDGAR release 22.4.1 on
2023-01-03, but nearly every reference still says thousands.

availableCommands.name: vitepress-mermaid-dark-mode-themevariables-leak
availableCommands.description:
Fix Mermaid diagrams in VitePress that look wrong in DARK mode — e.g. edge
labels rendered inside white boxes, or light node fills — even though the
diagram is fine in light mode. Use when: (1) using vitepress-plugin-mermaid
with `mermaid.themeVariables` configured, (2) dark-mode diagrams show white
`edgeLabelBackground` plates / light fills bleeding through, (3) toggling the
VitePress dark theme doesn't fully re-theme the diagram. Root cause: the plugin
forces mermaid's built-in `theme: "dark"` when `.dark` is present but STILL
applies your (light-tuned) themeVariables. Fix: override the affected pieces
with `.dark`-scoped CSS.

availableCommands.name: rails-default-scope-group-by-and-query-traps
availableCommands.description:
Cluster of ActiveRecord query bugs that pass silently in dev/empty DBs and then crash
or return wrong data at runtime against real data. Use when: (1) "PG::GroupingError:
column X must appear in the GROUP BY clause" from a .group() call, especially on a model
with a default_scope { order(...) } (the ordered column is INVISIBLE at the call site);
(2) a .select('DISTINCT ON ...') query that then calls .pluck and loses its distinctness;
(3) "ActiveModel::MissingAttributeError: missing attribute 'X'" after a partial
.select(...); (4) an N+1 where a model instance METHOD shadows a SQL SELECT alias of the
same name. Also covers reviewing read-only LLM/AI-agent "tool" classes for unbounded
result sets (provider 400 from context bloat), count-after-limit, and gating on the
wrong Pundit model. Triggers: Rails, ActiveRecord, Pundit, PostgreSQL, default_scope,
GROUP BY, DISTINCT ON, pluck, policy_scope.

availableCommands.name: change-event-drops-mouse-modifiers
availableCommands.description:
Fix checkbox/radio/select features driven by Alt, Shift, Ctrl or Meta that
silently stop working. Use when: (1) `event.altKey` / `event.shiftKey` /
`event.ctrlKey` / `event.metaKey` is `undefined` inside a handler,
(2) "Alt+Click to select all" or "Shift+Click to select a range" does nothing
while the control still ticks, (3) a modifier feature broke after a checkbox
was rewritten, a UI library was dropped, or a wrapper component was swapped to
a native `onchange` binding, (4) no error, no console warning -- the feature is
just inert, (5) a test asserting "disabled control does not fire" passes or
fails unexpectedly under `dispatchEvent`. Root cause: `change` is dispatched as
a plain `Event`, and modifier keys exist only on `MouseEvent`. Covers the
`click` binding fix and the `dispatchEvent` vs `.click()` difference on
disabled controls.

availableCommands.name: react-markdown-v10-code-blocks
availableCommands.description:
react-markdown v10 removed the `inline` prop from the `code` component, breaking
custom renderers that relied on it. Use when: (1) upgrading from react-markdown v8/v9
to v10 and `code` component shows TypeScript errors on `inline` prop, (2) trying to
style inline code differently from fenced code blocks, (3) `Unknown prop inline` warning
appears at runtime. Solution: check className?.startsWith('language-') to distinguish
block code (always has a language class) from inline code (never does). Override `pre`
for the block code container and `code` for both inline and block content.

availableCommands.name: mocha-config-leak-parent-worktree
availableCommands.description:
Fix mocha failing in a git worktree because it loaded a `.mocharc.*` from the
PARENT checkout. Use when: (1) `npm test` dies with
`Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../test/setup/register.js'
imported from <worktree>/` and that file does not exist on your branch,
(2) tests pass on `main` but explode in a worktree, or vice versa,
(3) mocha appears to load a setup/require/node-option you never configured,
(4) `ls .mocharc.*` in the worktree returns nothing yet mocha clearly read a
config, (5) a teammate merged a PR adding `.mocharc.json` and unrelated
worktrees started failing minutes later. Root cause: mocha resolves its config
by walking UP the directory tree, and a worktree under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`
or `<repo>/worktrees/` has the main checkout as an ancestor.

availableCommands.name: graphql-ruby-enum-token-names
availableCommands.description:
Fix graphql-ruby 2.x returning Ruby internal enum values ('active', 'InternalService')
instead of GraphQL token names ('ACTIVE', 'INTERNAL_SERVICE') in API responses.
Use when: (1) API responses contain lowercase/CamelCase enum values that don't match
the schema token names, (2) frontend string comparisons fail because API returns 'active'
but schema defines ACTIVE, (3) you want enum responses to be standard GraphQL tokens
so generated TypeScript types match wire values. Override BaseEnum.coerce_result to
return graphql_name instead of the Ruby internal value param.

availableCommands.name: daisyui-nested-theme-token-inversion
availableCommands.description:
Fix decorations that vanish or invert inside a nested DaisyUI `data-theme`
wrapper — a wave/curve SVG divider filled `fill-base-100`, a "cut-out" shape,
a scrim, or a faux page-background element. Use when: (1) a WaveDivider /
section-shape-divider is invisible after being placed inside a
`data-theme="my-dark-theme"` block, (2) an element meant to match the PAGE
background instead matches the dark section it sits in, (3) `bg-base-100` or
`fill-base-100` looks correct on one section and wrong on another,
(4) a divider that works under a `bg-primary` HeroBanner breaks when reused
under a nested-theme band. Root cause: `data-theme` REDEFINES the semantic
tokens for its whole subtree, so `base-100` inside a dark wrapper is the dark
colour, not the page colour — the shape paints dark-on-dark and disappears.
Fix: keep the decoration OUTSIDE the themed subtree (a light-themed `relative`
wrapper with the shape absolutely positioned over the band), so its tokens
resolve against the page theme.

availableCommands.name: rails-active-storage-svg-inline
availableCommands.description: Fix SVG images not displaying when served via Rails Active Storage. Use when: (1) tags show broken image icons for Active Storage SVG uploads, (2) curl shows content-type: application/octet-stream and content-disposition: attachment for SVG blobs, (3) SVG files upload successfully but don't render in the browser, (4) Active Storage serves SVGs as downloads instead of inline images. Root cause: Active Storage has TWO separate security lists that block SVG inline serving — both must be configured. Also covers Marcel content type misdetection for SVGs.

availableCommands.name: rails-sti-class-names-leaking
availableCommands.description:
Fix Rails STI class names (InternalService, ExternalService, AdditionalService)
leaking into UI display strings beyond the basic GraphQL enum field case.
Use when: (1) model name/display_name methods embed #{type} producing strings like
"[CONTRACT-001] ExternalService - City A | City B", (2) REST API controllers
serialize model.service_type directly as JSON bypassing GraphQL enum coerce_result,
(3) raw SQL SELECT services.type returns Ruby class names bypassing ActiveRecord STI.
Companion to graphql-ruby-enum-token-names skill which fixes typed enum fields.

availableCommands.name: npm-create-vite-nonempty-dir-wipes-files
availableCommands.description:
Prevents destroying an existing repo when scaffolding Vite into a directory that
already has files. Use when: (1) you need to run `npm create vite@latest .` in a
folder that already contains `.git/`, `docs/`, `.gitignore`, or other work, (2) the
scaffolder prompts "Current directory is not empty. Remove existing files and
continue?", (3) you're adding a Vite app to a pre-initialized git repo / greenfield
project that already has design docs, (4) any `create-*` / `degit` scaffolder that
offers to empty a non-empty target. Root cause: choosing "remove existing files"
deletes EVERYTHING including `.git/`. Fix: scaffold into a temp subdir and copy out,
never let the tool empty the real directory.

availableCommands.name: spa-fragment-links-never-scroll
availableCommands.description:
In-page `#heading` links set the URL fragment but do not scroll, in a SPA
whose content is fetched after mount and/or which uses a router that
intercepts anchor clicks. Use when: (1) clicking a table-of-contents entry
changes the address bar and nothing moves, (2) a deep link with a fragment
loads at the top of the page even though the element with that id exists,
(3) `window.scrollTo()` and `element.scrollIntoView()` both work when run by
hand, so the scroller is fine, (4) you are debugging anchors in Backstage,
react-aria RouterProvider, React Router, Next.js App Router, or any app that
renders markdown fetched over HTTP. Two independent causes usually apply at
once and fixing one leaves the link broken. Also covers scroll position
leaking across client-side page changes.

availableCommands.name: temporal-sethandler-let-narrowing-collapse
availableCommands.description:
Fix TypeScript "Property X does not exist on type 'never'" in Temporal workflow files
when removing non-null assertions on `let` variables that are reassigned by
`setHandler()` signal callbacks. Use when: (1) trying to replace `ciResult!.passed`
with a real null check and TS errors with TS2339 "Property 'passed' does not exist
on type 'never'", (2) `if (!x) throw` followed by `x.foo` errors with `never` type,
(3) the variable is declared `let x: T | null = null` and reassigned only inside a
`setHandler(signal, payload => { x = payload })` callback, (4) bumping
`noNonNullAssertion` to error in a Temporal workflow file. Root cause: TypeScript
control-flow analysis cannot see assignments that happen inside callbacks registered
with Temporal's `setHandler` (the SDK calls them later when a signal arrives), so the
variable's narrowed type stays at its literal `null` initializer. The non-null
assertion `x!` is the original workaround. To remove `!`, cast through the declared
union once: `const v = x as T | null; if (!v) throw ...; v.foo`.

availableCommands.name: fixed-timestep-cooldown-floor-drops-remainder
availableCommands.description:
Fixes rate-based timers (weapon fire rate, spawn rate, ability cooldowns) running
SLOWER than their configured rate in a fixed-timestep game/sim loop. Use when:
(1) a "12 rounds/sec" gun actually fires ~10/sec, (2) a cooldown is implemented as
`cd = Math.max(0, cd - dt)` then `if (ready) cd = 1/rate`, (3) the configured rate
constant doesn't match observed behavior, (4) any per-frame countdown that clamps to
zero each step and resets on fire. Root cause: clamping the timer to 0 each frame
discards the fractional overshoot, so the effective period is rounded UP to a whole
number of frames. Fix: carry the remainder (`cd += period`, compare `<= 0`) instead
of flooring.

availableCommands.name: yarn-4-foreach-include-scope-flag
availableCommands.description:
Fix Yarn 4 `workspaces foreach` failing with "Invalid option schema: missing
at least one property from `all`, `recursive`, `since`, or `worktree`" when
using `--include` (or `--exclude`) filters. Use when: (1) you write a root
monorepo script like
`yarn workspaces foreach -pi --include '@scope/api' --include '@scope/web' run dev`
and Yarn rejects it with the "Invalid option schema" usage error,
(2) you assumed `--include` alone scopes the run, the way it does in some
other monorepo runners (turbo, nx, pnpm `--filter`),
(3) the same script worked under Yarn 3 `workspaces foreach` plugin and
broke after upgrading to Yarn 4, (4) you're trying to spawn a parallel `dev`
fan-out across a subset of packages. Root cause: Yarn 4 requires you to
declare the *base* set of workspaces before applying filters; `--include` /
`--exclude` only narrow within a base set. The base set must be one of
`-A` / `--all`, `-R` / `--recursive`, `-W` / `--worktree`, or `--since`.
Fix: add `-A` (or whichever scope makes sense) BEFORE `--include`. The
practical canonical form for parallel dev runners is `-Api` (`--all`,
`--parallel`, `--interlaced`).

availableCommands.name: timescaledb-hypertable-on-conflict-pk
availableCommands.description:
Fix Postgres error 42P10 "there is no unique or exclusion constraint
matching the ON CONFLICT specification" when upserting into a TimescaleDB
hypertable (or any partitioned table). Use when: (1) an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT
(some_id) DO NOTHING/UPDATE throws 42P10 on a hypertable, (2) the column you
named IS the logical id but the upsert still fails, (3) a seed/ingest script
that worked on a plain table breaks after the table was converted to a
hypertable, (4) Prisma `$executeRaw` / driver-adapter surfaces
"DriverAdapterError: there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the
ON CONFLICT specification". Root cause: a hypertable's PK/unique constraint
MUST include the partitioning (time) column, so `ON CONFLICT (id)` alone
matches no constraint. Fix: list the FULL primary key in ON CONFLICT, e.g.
(partition_ts, id) — or whatever `\d table` reports as the PK.

availableCommands.name: threejs-setfromobject-skinned-gltf-oversized
availableCommands.description:
Fix for a rigged/skinned GLTF/GLB character that loads but is invisible (or
wrong size) because Box3().setFromObject() returns a bounding box far larger
than the visible mesh. Use when: (1) a SkinnedMesh model from GLTFLoader does
not appear even though it's in the scene, visible:true, has a skeleton, and is
not frustum-culled, (2) you auto-scale a character with
`scale = TARGET / (box.max.y - box.min.y)` and it comes out a tiny speck
(~1 cm) or gigantic, (3) measuring the model's rendered geometry shows it's
~100x off from the box you computed. Root cause: Box3.setFromObject walks the
armature/bones (Object3D nodes that can sit at large coordinates) and computes
deformed skinned bounds, so the box reflects bone extents, not the visible
mesh. Fix: measure from each mesh's geometry.boundingBox instead.

availableCommands.name: prisma-migrate-diff-split-themed-commits
availableCommands.description:
Generate Prisma migration SQL files OFFLINE (no DB, no Docker) when
splitting one working-tree `schema.prisma` change into multiple themed
commits, each with its own migration. Use when: (1) you have several
unrelated edits piled into a single `schema.prisma` (new column +
new indexes + new model) and want to land them as separate commits
with separate, timestamped migration files, (2) you don't have a
running database (Docker is off, CI hasn't provisioned one, you're
on the train), (3) `prisma migrate dev` errors with
`P1001: Can't reach database server`, (4) `prisma migrate diff
--from-migrations` errors with `You must set
datasource.shadowDatabaseUrl in your prisma.config.ts if you want
to diff a migrations directory`. Root cause: `--from-migrations`
needs a live shadow DB to replay migrations, but the schema-to-schema
form `--from-schema A --to-schema B --script` does NOT need any DB —
it diffs two file inputs directly and emits SQL on stdout. The trick
is to manufacture intermediate schema files for each theme and chain
diffs between consecutive pairs. Also covers the Prisma 7 rename
`--to-schema-datamodel` → `--to-schema`.

availableCommands.name: php-json-encode-inside-html-event-attribute
availableCommands.description:
Fix PHP templates that inject json_encode() output into a double-quoted HTML event
attribute (onmouseover="return overlib(<?php echo json_encode($x) ?>, …)"). Symptoms:
(1) fragments like `<\/td><\/tr>", CAPTION, "Checked Out", BELOW, RIGHT);" onMouseOut="return nd();"/>`
appear as visible text in a table row, (2) cells shift / the row after a tooltip icon is
mangled, (3) a JS handler "escaped for safety" now breaks the markup. Root cause:
json_encode emits `"` which terminates the attribute; `\/` is JSON slash escaping.
Fix: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) the whole JS expression before placing it in the
attribute — browsers HTML-decode attribute values before executing the handler.

availableCommands.name: yarn-4-bin-resolution-workspace
availableCommands.description:
Fix CI / npm-script failure `Usage Error: Couldn't find a script named "<bin>"`
when invoking a binary that lives in a child workspace via the root, e.g.
`yarn playwright install`, `yarn prisma migrate`, `yarn tsc`, `yarn vitest`,
in a Yarn 4 monorepo. Use when: (1) a GitHub Actions / GitLab CI step that
previously worked under Yarn Classic / npm now fails after a Yarn 4 upgrade,
(2) the error message points at the binary name as if it were a typo, but
the binary is installed only in a child workspace (`apps/backend`,
`packages/web`, etc.) and not declared at the root, (3) `yarn install`
succeeds, `yarn workspace <name> exec <bin>` works, but plain `yarn <bin>`
fails. Root cause: Yarn 4 narrowed `yarn <name>` semantics to "run a script
named <name>" — it no longer falls back to resolving `<name>` as a binary
shipped by a nested workspace the way Yarn 1 (Classic) did. Fix: run the
binary inside its owning workspace with `yarn workspace <pkg-name> exec
<bin> <args...>` (or use `yarn dlx` if you don't want a local install at
all).

availableCommands.name: backstage-search-result-absolute-location-new-tab
availableCommands.description:
Backstage search results that open in a new browser tab, labelled "Opens in
a new window", because the collator set an absolute URL as the document
`location`. Use when: (1) clicking a search result leaves the app instead of
navigating client-side, (2) your collator builds locations from
`app.baseUrl`, (3) results from a custom collator behave differently from
catalog results. Also covers making a custom document type filterable and
legible: results render with the generic item and cannot be narrowed to
unless the plugin contributes SearchFilterResultTypeBlueprint and
SearchResultListItemBlueprint.

availableCommands.name: paperclip-create-plugin
availableCommands.description: Create new Paperclip plugins with the current alpha SDK/runtime. Use when scaffolding a plugin package, adding a new example plugin, or updating plugin authoring docs. Covers the supported worker/UI surface, route conventions, scaffold flow, and verification steps.

availableCommands.name: apparent-hang-is-slow-noprogress-download
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose and fix a CLI/tool command that "hangs" while downloading — especially
self-update / install commands pulling a multi-MB binary. Use when: (1) a
command with a network download appears frozen with no output, (2) users report
"update is not working" / "it just hangs", (3) a fetch-then-write has no progress
indicator and no timeout. The usual root cause is NOT a code freeze but a
slow-but-progressing large download over variable CDN throughput, silently
streaming with zero feedback, so the user Ctrl-C's it. Covers bisecting the
network path, confirming it's environmental (not a bug), and the streaming fix
(per-chunk stall timeout + progress line, not a total timeout).

availableCommands.name: find-skills
availableCommands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

availableCommands.name: claude-code-docker-native-install
availableCommands.description:
Fix for Claude Code auto-update failures in Docker containers. Use when:
(1) claude auto-update fails with permission denied or requires sudo,
(2) Dockerfile uses `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` and container
drops to a non-root user, (3) upgrading a ccpod-style image where claude runs
as a non-root user. Claude Code migrated from npm-global to a native binary
installer (curl install.sh) that installs to ~/.local/bin — user-writable and
auto-update compatible.

availableCommands.name: docker-bind-mount-stale-after-host-rmrf
availableCommands.description:
Deleting and recreating a bind-mounted directory ON THE HOST while the
container runs leaves the container bound to the deleted inode: it sees an
EMPTY directory, its writes never reach the host, and nothing reports an
error. Use when: (1) a test/verification script does `rm -rf ./data && mkdir`
between runs and the next run behaves as if no files exist, (2) a job that
scans a mounted directory reports zero items — "0 backups", "nothing to
prune", "no input files" — when the host clearly has files, (3) files written
by the container stop appearing on the host, or vice versa, (4) `docker exec
... ls /mnt` is empty but `ls ./data` on the host is not, (5) a redirect
inside the container fails with "I/O error" or "No such file or directory" on
a path that exists on the host, (6) you are about to debug an application as
if it lost its data when only the mount went stale. Fix is a container
restart; the durable fix is to empty the directory contents rather than
replace the directory.

availableCommands.name: prisma-upgrade-v7
availableCommands.description: Complete migration guide from Prisma ORM v6 to v7 covering all breaking changes. Use when upgrading Prisma versions, encountering v7 errors, or migrating existing projects. Triggers on "upgrade to prisma 7", "prisma 7 migration", "prisma-client generator", "driver adapter required".

availableCommands.name: biome-nested-root-config-blocks-lint
availableCommands.description:
Biome refuses to run — not "runs slowly", refuses — when a second checkout
containing its own biome.json sits inside the repo, e.g. a git worktree under
`.claude/worktrees/` created for an isolated agent run. Use when: (1) `yarn
lint` / `biome check` dies with "Found a nested root configuration, but
there's already a root configuration", (2) linting broke the moment a
parallel agent or worktree started, and works again once it finishes,
(3) `git status` suddenly shows tens of thousands of untracked files,
(4) CI passes but the same command fails locally, (5) you are about to add
worktree isolation to a repo that has a root-level tool config. Root cause:
the parent's tooling scans DOWN into the nested checkout and finds a
competing root config. Fix: ignore the worktree directory in both the tool
config and .gitignore.

availableCommands.name: rails-sti-habtm-base-class-eager-load
availableCommands.description:
Fix ActiveRecord::AssociationNotFoundError when calling includes() on a STI base
class scope where only some subclasses define has_and_belongs_to_many. Use when:
(1) InternalService/ExternalService have HABTM but AdditionalService doesn't,
(2) includes(:drivers) on Service.all raises AssociationNotFoundError,
(3) ServiceType GraphQL resolver fires N+1 per node because association isn't
preloaded. Solution: move the HABTM declaration to the STI base class so includes()
works uniformly; subclasses without join-table data simply get an empty collection.

availableCommands.name: npm-first-publish-always-sets-latest
availableCommands.description:
`npm publish --tag next` still sets `latest` when it is a package's FIRST
published version, so a prerelease or placeholder becomes what everyone
installs by default. Use when: (1) you published with a dist-tag and
`npm view <pkg> dist-tags` shows `latest` pointing at it anyway, (2) you
intended nothing to resolve from a bare `npm install` while an API settles,
(3) a placeholder version like 0.0.0 reached the registry, (4) you need to
recover: unpublish rules, the 72-hour window, and why the ORDER of
republish-then-unpublish matters, (5) you are planning a first release under
a `next`/`beta` tag. Root cause: a package must have a `latest`, so npm
assigns the first version to it regardless of `--tag`; `latest` also cannot
be removed, only repointed.

availableCommands.name: nextjs-font-axes-weight-conflict
availableCommands.description:
Fix the next/font/google build error "Axes can only be defined for variable
fonts when the weight property is nonexistent or set to `variable`". Use when:
(1) next build / next dev fails with "Module not found: Can't resolve
'next/font/google/target.css'" whose root cause line is the Axes message,
(2) you configured a variable Google font (e.g. Fraunces, Inter, Recursive)
with BOTH `axes: [...]` and an explicit `weight: [...]` array, (3) you want
optical-size / SOFT / other named axes on a variable font. Root cause:
next/font forbids combining `axes` with a fixed `weight` list — a variable
font must omit `weight` (or set weight: 'variable') so the full wght axis is
loaded, which still exposes every weight to Tailwind font-weight utilities.

availableCommands.name: busybox-run-parts-executes-dotted-strays
availableCommands.description:
BusyBox `run-parts` (Alpine) executes `job.bak`, `job.orig` and `job~`;
Debian's `run-parts` skips them. So an editor backup, a `sed -i.bak`, or a
merge leftover in /etc/periodic/* or /etc/cron.daily becomes a SCHEDULED
TASK on Alpine, silently running stale code. Use when: (1) a cron job in an
Alpine container appears to run twice, or a concurrency/flock guard reports
"already running" every night, (2) a scheduled task alerts as failed nightly
but works when run by hand, (3) you are about to `sed -i.bak` or leave a
`.orig` in a directory that run-parts scans, (4) you are writing or
reviewing a task-runner container that bind-mounts a directory of scripts,
(5) a script that "was reverted" is still running in production, (6) a
validator that globs the same task directory reads a stale value from a
backup file and reports a false pass. Also covers why a `.sql` or config
file sitting beside its script is safe only because it is non-executable.

availableCommands.name: gh-pr-create-fork-parent-default
availableCommands.description:
Fix `gh pr create` failing on a FORK with the misleading error
"No commits between main and <branch>" / "Head sha can't be blank, Base sha
can't be blank" / "Head ref must be a branch (createPullRequest)". Use when:
(1) you just pushed a branch successfully but `gh pr create` insists there are
no commits, (2) `git log origin/main..HEAD` clearly shows commits yet gh
disagrees, (3) retrying the command changes nothing, (4) you are working in a
repo created with "Fork" on GitHub, (5) you are about to open a PR against
your OWN fork and must not accidentally target the upstream parent. Root cause:
gh defaults the BASE repo of a PR to the fork's PARENT, not your fork.

availableCommands.name: native-crash-faulting-thread-not-loaded-modules
availableCommands.description:
A native module named in a crash report is usually just LOADED, not guilty. Culpability
is decided by which binaries appear in the FAULTING THREAD's frames — parse them before
blaming anything. Use when: (1) a Node/Electron process dies with SIGSEGV/SIGABRT/
EXC_BAD_ACCESS and no JS stack, (2) a native addon (better-sqlite3, sharp, canvas,
node-gyp builds) is present and is the obvious suspect, (3) jest/mocha reports a worker
crash naming an innocent-looking test file, (4) you are about to pin/downgrade a native
dep on a hunch. Covers parsing macOS .ips JSON crash reports to extract the faulting
thread, and recognising V8 GC frames (ClearStaleLeftTrimmedPointerVisitor, MarkCompact,
Sparkplug/BaselineOutOfLinePrologue) that indicate an upstream V8 bug, not your code.

availableCommands.name: paperclip-create-agent
availableCommands.description: Create new agents in Paperclip with governance-aware hiring. Use when you need to inspect adapter configuration options, compare existing agent configs, draft a new agent prompt/config, and submit a hire request.

availableCommands.name: zustand-v5-selector-new-reference-loop
availableCommands.description:
Fix "Maximum update depth exceeded" / infinite re-render caused by a zustand
v5 selector that returns a NEW reference each call. Use when: (1) a component
or hook using useStore/useAuthStore throws "Maximum update depth exceeded.
This can happen when a component repeatedly calls setState...", (2) the stack
trace goes through forceStoreRerender / updateStoreInstance /
useSyncExternalStore, (3) the selector contains a fallback like
`(s) => s.user?.roles ?? []` or returns an inline object/array literal
`(s) => ({ a: s.a, b: s.b })` or `(s) => s.items.map(...)`, (4) the loop only
triggers on a specific state (e.g. when a value is null and the `?? []`
branch runs). Root cause: zustand v5 compares snapshots with Object.is and
dropped v4's auto-caching, so a fresh reference every render makes
useSyncExternalStore re-render on every commit. Fix: return a stable
reference (module-level constant) or use useShallow.

availableCommands.name: better-auth-redirectplugin-signin-redirect-loop
availableCommands.description:
Fix for login redirect loop when using Better Auth email+password sign-in in Next.js.
Use when: (1) user logs in with correct credentials but gets redirected back to the login page,
(2) portal/app routes immediately redirect to login after a successful auth response,
(3) signIn.email() or signUp.email() includes a callbackURL parameter.
Root cause: Better Auth's default redirectPlugin fires window.location.href before the
browser commits the Set-Cookie header, so the next request arrives without the session cookie.

availableCommands.name: fs-mtime-rounds-ahead-of-datenow
availableCommands.description:
A file's `stat().mtime.getTime()` can read up to 1ms AHEAD of a `Date.now()` taken
immediately AFTER the write — measured at ~49% of writes on macOS/APFS. Node builds
`stat.mtime` from the raw nanosecond timespec and ROUNDS to the nearest millisecond,
while `Date.now()` truncates. Use when: (1) an age/staleness check written as
`mtime > now` or `now - mtime > 0` behaves inconsistently, (2) a cache/GC/cleanup test
that "should collect everything" flakes at roughly 25-50%, (3) code computes an age
that can come out NEGATIVE and you assumed it could not, (4) a `maxAge: 0` /
`--min-age 0` / "no minimum" option silently fails to include just-written files,
(5) you are comparing any filesystem or remote-object timestamp against a locally
read clock. Fix: clamp with `Math.max(0, now - mtime)` and compare `age < minAge`,
never `mtime > cutoff`.

availableCommands.name: mariadb-slow-query-log-silently-disabled
availableCommands.description:
Explains why a MariaDB/MySQL slow query log file is empty or missing even though
SHOW VARIABLES reports slow_query_log = ON. Use when: (1) slow_query_log_file
points somewhere that contains no file at all, (2) the Slow_queries status counter
climbs into the thousands but nothing is ever written, (3) the log directory is a
Docker bind mount and stays empty, (4) you are about to conclude "we have no slow
queries" or "logging is enabled, so the log must be elsewhere". Root cause is
usually "Turning logging off for the whole duration of the MariaDB server process"
after Errcode 13 permission denied at startup, typically a bind-mount owned by the
wrong uid. Covers why SHOW VARIABLES cannot be trusted here.

availableCommands.name: openobserve-meta-store-silently-ignored
availableCommands.description:
OpenObserve silently ignores ZO_META_POSTGRES_DSN (or ZO_META_MYSQL_DSN) unless
ZO_META_STORE is also set, writing metadata to SQLite instead. Use when:
(1) wiring OpenObserve to Postgres/MySQL in docker-compose, Kubernetes, or any
self-hosted deployment, (2) the Postgres container attached to OpenObserve stays
empty — "Did not find any relations" / zero rows — while the app reports healthy,
(3) OpenObserve dashboards, users or alerts vanish after restoring a database
backup, (4) reviewing an OpenObserve stack for correctness. Also covers why
ZO_S3_* variables do nothing (ZO_LOCAL_MODE_STORAGE must be s3) and why a Docker
healthcheck on /healthz always reports unhealthy (the image is distroless).

availableCommands.name: vercel-composition-patterns
availableCommands.description: React composition patterns that scale. Use when refactoring components with boolean prop proliferation, building flexible component libraries, or designing reusable APIs. Triggers on tasks involving compound components, render props, context providers, or component architecture. Includes React 19 API changes.

availableCommands.name: rubocop-yoda-array-concat-reorder
availableCommands.description:
Rubocop Style/YodaExpression false-fires on order-sensitive `+` expressions like
`CONST_ARRAY + method_call` ("Non-literal operand should be first") and its
AUTOCORRECT swaps the operands — silently changing program behavior when the
concatenation order matters (precedence lists, prepend semantics, string concat).
Use when: (1) rubocop flags Style/YodaExpression on a line with `+` and no
comparison, (2) `rubocop -A` reordered an array/string concatenation and a
lookup/precedence test started failing, (3) deciding whether to autocorrect or
inline-disable. Fix: inline-disable with a justifying comment; never autocorrect
an order-sensitive concatenation.

availableCommands.name: fastify-cors-missing-put-delete-methods
availableCommands.description:
Fix for CORS errors on PUT/DELETE/PATCH requests when using @fastify/cors.
Use when: (1) browser DevTools shows a 204 preflight AND a "CORS error" for
the same URL simultaneously, (2) GET/POST to the same endpoint work fine but
mutations fail, (3) the @fastify/cors registration has no explicit `methods`
option. Root cause: @fastify/cors defaults to methods:'GET,HEAD,POST' — the
OPTIONS handler returns 204 unconditionally, but the response's
Access-Control-Allow-Methods header only lists GET,HEAD,POST, so the browser
blocks any PUT/DELETE/PATCH with a CORS policy violation.

availableCommands.name: biome-exhaustive-deps-optional-chaining
availableCommands.description:
Fix Biome useExhaustiveDependencies errors when useMemo/useCallback deps use
optional chaining (e.g. [obj?.nested]). Biome raises TWO errors: "dependency
more specific than its captures: obj?.nested" AND "does not specify dependency
on obj". Use when: (1) useMemo dep list uses optional chaining like run?.specSnapshot,
(2) you get both the "more specific" and "missing dep" violations simultaneously,
(3) you intentionally want to key on a nested stable property to avoid recomputing
when sibling properties change.

availableCommands.name: nested-worktree-resolves-parent-node-modules
availableCommands.description:
Detect verification that silently ran against the WRONG source tree because a
git worktree created INSIDE the main repo (e.g. `.claude/worktrees/agent-*/`,
`.worktrees/foo/`) has no `node_modules` of its own, so Node/Bun resolution
walks up and finds the parent checkout's. Use when: (1) an agent or teammate
reports "all gates green" in a worktree that has no `node_modules`, (2)
typecheck passes in a worktree but the same commit fails on CI or after merge,
(3) a monorepo workspace import (`@scope/pkg`) resolves to the parent
checkout's source rather than the worktree's edited copy, (4) tsc reports
"phantom" errors in a worktree referencing code you already changed, (5) a
worktree run mysteriously succeeds when `biome` / `turbo` / `vitest` are not
installed in it. Root cause: node resolution ascends parent directories, and a
nested worktree's parent IS a checkout with a populated `node_modules` — so
binaries are found and workspace packages resolve to the WRONG tree, with no
error. Fix: run the package manager's install inside each worktree, and treat
a missing `node_modules` as invalidating any gate result from it.

availableCommands.name: riot-observable-resubscribe-onupdated
availableCommands.description:
Fix Riot.js components that accumulate duplicate event listeners because they
subscribe from `onUpdated`. Use when: (1) a component calls
`props.model.on('event', ...)` from `onUpdated`/`onMounted` and the list gets
slower the more you sort, search, or paginate, (2) one async response triggers
many `update()` calls on the same component, (3) a guard like
`if (typeof props.x.size === 'number') return` or `if (props.x !== state.x)`
exists but does not hold while a request is still in flight, (4) sorting a
table during load makes the UI progressively jankier, (5) you need to measure
listener accumulation but `@riotjs/observable` stores callbacks in a
closure-private Map you cannot inspect. Root cause: `onUpdated` runs on every
render, and a guard that only becomes true once the response lands leaves the
in-flight window unguarded.

availableCommands.name: docker-gosu-env-path-not-inherited
availableCommands.description:
Fix "command: not found" errors inside Docker containers when invoking tools via
`gosu user-switch` from an entrypoint script, even though the tool was installed
and `ENV PATH=...` was set in the Dockerfile. Use when: (1) Dockerfile has
`ENV PATH="/some/bin:${PATH}"` but binary isn't found at runtime through
`gosu user sh -c '...'`, (2) image rebuild does not fix the missing tool,
(3) entrypoint runs as root and drops to non-root via `gosu` before executing
user/init scripts. Root cause: Docker sets ENV only on the main process; user-
switch tools (gosu, su, sudo) do not reliably forward PATH across the boundary.

availableCommands.name: node-buffer-base64-silent-decode
availableCommands.description:
Node.js Buffer.from(str, 'base64') never throws on invalid base64 — it silently
ignores invalid characters and decodes what it can. Use when: (1) implementing
base64 input validation, (2) expecting Buffer.from to throw on malformed input,
(3) building import/decode flows that need to reject bad base64. Validate at the
parse/schema layer instead of the decode layer.

availableCommands.name: vitest-lazy-imports-slower-in-full-suite
availableCommands.description:
Avoid a Vitest "optimisation" that makes the targeted tests much faster and the
whole suite slower. Use when: (1) profiling a Vitest suite whose summary shows
`import` far exceeding `tests` (module-graph re-execution, not slow
assertions), (2) you are about to replace static imports with `await import()`
so each test file loads only its own subtree, (3) a per-file microbenchmark
says 2x faster and you have not yet measured the full `yarn test`, (4) you are
considering `--no-isolate`, `--pool=threads`, or `deps.optimizer` to speed up
Vitest. Root cause: Vitest gives each test file its own module registry, so a
shared graph is re-executed per file — but converting to runtime dynamic
