imports moves that cost onto Vite's transform pipeline, where many workers
contend, and the whole suite gets SLOWER even as summed import time collapses.

availableCommands.name: rebase-structure-sql-drops-schema-migrations
availableCommands.description:
A `git rebase` (or merge) auto-merge of a Rails SQL-format `db/structure.sql`
can SILENTLY drop schema_migrations rows (and their schema objects) that landed
on the base branch while your feature branch was open — no conflict markers,
clean rebase, wrong result. Use when: (1) after rebasing a long-lived branch
onto main, `db/structure.sql` is missing migration version rows that exist on
origin/main, (2) `bin/rails test` aborts with "Migrations are pending ... You
have N pending migration" for a migration FILE that came from main, (3) you
used `config.active_record.schema_format = :sql` (structure.sql, not schema.rb),
(4) an early commit on your branch had regenerated structure.sql so the rebase
replaced the whole schema_migrations region with your branch's stale copy.
Root cause: structure.sql's schema_migrations INSERT list and DDL are one
contiguous generated region; whichever side's commit last rewrote it wins the
auto-merge, dropping the other side's rows. Fix: rebuild from origin/main's
exact structure.sql + re-apply ONLY your migration's deltas, or regenerate
authoritatively on a throwaway DB. Verify by loading into a scratch DB.

availableCommands.name: vitepress-preview-stale-chunks-after-rebuild
availableCommands.description:
Fix a VitePress site that loads but doesn't hydrate — Mermaid diagrams stay
blank, local search is dead, `window.mermaid` is undefined — with the browser
console showing 404s for `app.*.js` / `theme.*.js`. Use when: (1) you ran
`vitepress build` while a `vitepress preview` server was already running,
(2) SSR content (feature icons, prose) shows but anything needing JS is dead,
(3) hashed chunk files 404. Root cause: a rebuild produces new content-hashed
chunk names; the already-running preview server serves HTML referencing the new
hashes but 404s the files. Fix: restart `vitepress preview` after every build.

availableCommands.name: worktree-typecheck-wrong-directory
availableCommands.description:
Fix for TypeScript typecheck silently running on the main project instead of a
git worktree. Use when: (1) `yarn workspace frontend typecheck` reports zero errors
but CI fails with TypeScript errors from files you modified in a worktree,
(2) tsc appears to pass but changes in the worktree aren't being checked,
(3) you're debugging TypeScript errors in a monorepo worktree setup where
node_modules lives in the main project root, not the worktree.

availableCommands.name: node-domexception-invalid-this
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose and fix Node's `TypeError: Value of "this" must be of DOMException`
(ERR_INVALID_THIS), and the related `Cannot read private member #x from an
object whose class did not declare it`. Use when: (1) a job/run record or
crash report stores exactly `Value of "this" must be of DOMException` with no
other context, (2) a **logging call itself throws** — stack shows pino /
`@pinojs/redact` / `fast-redact`, `traverse`, `redactWildcardPath`, or
`_asJson`, (3) an error surfaces only in production but never in dev or tests,
(4) a `catch` block or error-reporting path throws instead of reporting the
real failure, (5) you suspect an `AbortController` / `AbortSignal.timeout` /
`fetch` abort but the abort path itself looks correct, (6) any code does
`Object.create(Object.getPrototypeOf(err))` then reads `.name`/`.message`.
Covers the log-redaction root cause, why a *genuine* DOMException triggers it,
which properties are brand-checked, and the safe-describe pattern.

availableCommands.name: ci-test-sharding-economics
availableCommands.description:
Split a slow CI test suite across parallel jobs WITHOUT making it slower or
breaking the coverage gate. Use when: (1) adding `parallel:` / matrix sharding
to a GitLab or GitHub test job, (2) every shard fails with "Coverage for lines
(44.53%) does not meet global threshold (86%)" or similar — each shard ran a
fraction of the files, (3) you sharded and the stage got SLOWER, (4) a shard
sits queued for minutes before starting, (5) you need `vitest --shard` to still
enforce coverage thresholds over the whole suite, (6) you are choosing a shard
count and about to pick 4 because it looks tidy. Covers the blob-report/merge
recipe, why `--coverage` enforces as well as collects, and why more shards than
the fleet can run concurrently is strictly worse than fewer.

availableCommands.name: next-upgrade
availableCommands.description: Upgrade Next.js to the latest version following official migration guides and codemods

availableCommands.name: fk-to-habtm-stale-column
availableCommands.description:
Fix stale data when migrating a Rails model from a belongs_to FK column (e.g.
driver_id) to a has_and_belongs_to_many join table. Use when: (1) GraphQL API
switches from driverId to driverIds input but existing callers (notification
mutations, assistant tools, resolver queries) still read the FK column and get
stale/ghost data, (2) notifyDriver sends SMS to the wrong driver after reassignment,
(3) DriverType.services OR-query returns ghost services for de-assigned drivers.
Core fix: after any HABTM assignment, explicitly null the FK column so there is a
single source of truth.

availableCommands.name: git-worktree-remove-directory-not-empty
availableCommands.description:
Fix `git worktree remove` failing with "fatal: failed to delete '<path>':
Directory not empty" caused by gitignored build artifacts (node_modules,
.astro, .next, dist, target, __pycache__, .venv) left behind by an install
or build run inside the worktree. Use when: (1) worktree cleanup aborts with
"Directory not empty" even with --force, (2) after the failure `git worktree
list` no longer shows the worktree but the directory still exists on disk,
(3) `git worktree prune` reports nothing to do and the orphan directory
remains, (4) cleaning up agent/task worktrees under .worktrees/ or
.claude/worktrees/ where dependencies were installed. Key insight: the
removal is NOT atomic — it deregisters the worktree and deletes most content
BEFORE failing, so the usual "prune it" advice cannot help and a plain
`rm -rf` is the remaining step. NOT for the submodule variant ("working trees
containing submodules cannot be moved or removed") — see
git-worktrees-with-submodules.

availableCommands.name: stacked-branches-rebase-after-squash-merge
availableCommands.description:
Rebase a chain of stacked MR/PR branches after the bottom of the stack was SQUASH-merged
into main. Use when: (1) every branch in the stack shows "ahead N, behind 2" and a plain
`git rebase main` replays already-merged commits and conflicts on files the merged MR
touched, (2) rebasing the top branch tries to replay 20-30 commits instead of its own 1-4,
(3) `git rebase <new-parent-branch>` on a stacked branch falls back to the original fork
point because every ancestor SHA was rewritten by earlier rebases in the chain, (4) a
branch in the stack contains a merge commit of a sibling branch (cannot be flattened by
rebase). Fix: rebase each level bottom-up with `git rebase --onto <new-base> <old-base-tip>
<branch>`, recording old tips first; rebuild merge-containing branches with checkout -B +
merge + cherry-pick; verify `git rev-list --count new-base..HEAD` equals the branch's own
commit count before force-pushing.

availableCommands.name: git-merge-stale-stat-cache-false-conflict
availableCommands.description:
Fix `git merge`/`git checkout`/`git rebase` refusing to run with "Your local
changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge" when the file is
NOT actually modified. Use when: (1) git names a file as locally changed but
`git status` reports a clean tree, (2) `git diff <file>` shows nothing yet the
merge still aborts, (3) the named file is a build artifact or lockfile that a
recent `npm install` / `npm run build` / formatter touched, (4) "Aborting"
appears alongside "Updating <a>..<b>" and you are about to `git checkout --` or
`reset --hard` a file you would rather not discard. Root cause is a stale index
stat cache: git compares mtime/size before content, so a rewrite with identical
bytes still looks modified until the index is refreshed.

availableCommands.name: prisma-7-database-url-resolution
availableCommands.description:
Fix `PrismaConfigEnvError: Cannot resolve environment variable: DATABASE_URL`
thrown when `prisma.config.ts` loads. Covers two contexts that share the same
root cause but need different fixes: (A) CI — no `.env` exists at all, and
`prisma generate` fails even though it doesn't need a DB connection; (B)
monorepo dev — `.env` lives at the repo root but `yarn workspace @scope/pkg
prisma ...` runs with cwd = the workspace subdir, so the root `.env` is never
auto-loaded, and dotenv v17 also doesn't expand `${VAR}` interpolation. Use
when: (1) any `prisma` command fails immediately with
`Failed to load config file ".../packages/<x>" as a TypeScript/JavaScript
module. Error: PrismaConfigEnvError: Cannot resolve environment variable:
DATABASE_URL.`, (2) the same command works when prefixed with an inline
`DATABASE_URL=...` or `dotenv -e .env --`, (3) local dev works but CI fails
the same step, (4) upgrading Prisma 5/6 → 7 and the old "auto-load .env from
cwd and parents" behavior is gone. Root cause: in Prisma 7 the URL moved
out of `schema.prisma` into `prisma.config.ts`, and `env('DATABASE_URL')` is
resolved EAGERLY at config-file load — even for commands like `generate`
that don't connect.

availableCommands.name: promise-over-task-queue-drop-strands-callers
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose a UI that hangs forever in a pending state — a modal stuck on
"Saving…"/"Deleting…" with its cancel button disabled, a spinner that never
resolves — after some unrelated action cancelled in-flight work. Use when:
(1) an `await` never returns and no error is thrown or logged, (2) a
concurrency limiter / request pool / job queue has a `drop()`, `clear()`,
`abort()` or `cancelAll()` that does `this.queue = []`, (3) a promise wraps a
callback-style `submit(task)` whose completion callback is only reachable from
inside the task body, (4) the hang only reproduces when one flow is cancelled
while another is mid-operation, (5) a mocha/jest regression test for it fails
by TIMEOUT rather than by assertion. Root cause: a dropped task never runs, so
it never reaches the `done`/`loadend` that settles the promise, and the caller
waits for the life of the page. Fix: make cancellation a notification, not a
deletion — `submit(task, onDrop)` and have `drop()` invoke every `onDrop`.

availableCommands.name: vexor-cli
availableCommands.description: Semantic file discovery via `vexor`. Use whenever locating where something is implemented/loaded/defined in a medium or large repo, or when the file location is unclear. Prefer this over manual browsing.

availableCommands.name: distroless-healthcheck-exec-form
availableCommands.description:
Add a working Docker healthcheck to a distroless / shell-less image by using exec-form
CMD with an interpreter the image already ships, instead of giving up on healthchecks.
Use when: (1) a container is permanently `unhealthy` with empty healthcheck output,
(2) `docker exec <c> /bin/sh` fails with `exec: "/bin/sh": stat /bin/sh: no such file
or directory`, (3) the image has no curl, wget or nc so the usual
`CMD-SHELL curl -f http://localhost/health` cannot run, (4) you read advice saying
"this image is distroless, do not add a healthcheck" and want to check whether that is
actually true for your image. Covers CMD vs CMD-SHELL, choosing a version-independent
binary name, and distinguishing a failing probe from a crash-looping app.

availableCommands.name: riot-rollup-dist-nondeterministic-expr-ids
availableCommands.description:
Explains why a committed Riot.js + Rollup `dist/` bundle shows a diff after
rebuilding identical source, and how to compare two bundles meaningfully.
Use when: (1) `npm run build` on a clean tree leaves `dist/` modified with
no source change, (2) two consecutive builds produce different md5 hashes,
(3) a diff of the minified bundle shows only `expr51` -> `expr65` style
renumbering, (4) you are about to chase a phantom "stale dist" bug or add
dist to a bisect. Root cause: the Riot compiler assigns `exprNN` ids from a
bundle-global counter and Rollup's module transform order is unstable;
`maxParallelFileOps: 1` does NOT fix it. Normalize with
`sed -E 's/expr[0-9]+/exprN/g'` before hashing. Also covers deciding whether
a committed `dist/` may be untracked: check GitHub Pages (`_config.yml`,
`demo/` loading `../dist/`) and not just CI/Docker, because Pages
"deploy from a branch" serves the committed bundle with no build step.

availableCommands.name: turbopack-nft-process-cwd-warning
availableCommands.description:
Fix for Turbopack build warning: "Encountered unexpected file in NFT list / A file was traced
that indicates that the whole project was traced unintentionally." Triggered by process.cwd()
inside fs/path operations in server-side code imported by Next.js routes with output: 'standalone'.
Three approaches that DO NOT work: turbopackIgnore comment, import.meta.dirname, import.meta.url.
The fix is outputFileTracingExcludes in next.config.ts.

availableCommands.name: opentelemetry-resources-v2-factory
availableCommands.description:
Fix `error TS2693: 'Resource' only refers to a type, but is being used as
a value here.` after upgrading `@opentelemetry/resources` from `1.x` to
`2.x`. Use when: (1) bumping `@opentelemetry/resources` to `2.x` (or
pulling it transitively via `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` `0.55+`,
`@opentelemetry/sdk-logs`, etc.), (2) `tsc` fails on a line like
`new Resource({ [ATTR_SERVICE_NAME]: ... })`, (3) a pre-existing
TS2741 error
`Property 'getRawAttributes' is missing in type ... Resource ... required
in type ... Resource` shows up because two copies of `@opentelemetry/resources`
(v1 + v2) were dragged in by transitive deps. Root cause: in
`@opentelemetry/resources` v2 the `Resource` class constructor was
removed; `Resource` is now exported as a `type` only, and instances must
be created via the factory `resourceFromAttributes()` (or the related
`defaultResource()`, `emptyResource()`, `detectResources()` helpers).

availableCommands.name: fastify-ajv-coerces-null-to-empty-string
availableCommands.description:
Fix a Fastify PATCH/POST body where a JSON `null` arrives in the handler as an
empty string `''`. Use when: (1) a "send null to clear this field" API stores
`""` instead of `NULL`, (2) `request.body.x` is `''` and `typeof` is `'string'`
after the client demonstrably sent `null`, (3) one nullable field in a request
arrives as `null` while another in the SAME request arrives as `''`, (4) a
TypeBox `Type.Union([Type.String(), Type.Null()])` body field behaves
inconsistently depending on whether the string branch declares a `format`.
Root cause: Fastify runs ajv with `coerceTypes` enabled, which coerces `null`
to `''` against a `string | null` union — but not when the string branch
carries a format the empty string fails, where the null branch matches
instead. Includes why disabling coercion globally is the wrong fix.

availableCommands.name: react-resizable-panels-v4-size-units
availableCommands.description:
Fix collapsed `<Panel>` widths in react-resizable-panels v4. Use when: (1) `<Panel defaultSize={20}>`
renders ~20 pixels wide instead of 20% of the parent group, (2) sidebar / pipeline panels collapse
to slivers showing only truncated labels while one panel (usually the middle) eats the rest of
the screen, (3) `minSize` / `maxSize` constraints appear ignored, (4) you upgraded
`react-resizable-panels` from v2 / v3 to v4+ and the layout broke without any code change. Root
cause: v4's `bt()` size parser interprets bare `number` props as PIXELS; v2/v3 treated them as
percentages. Strings ending in `%` (e.g. `"20%"`) work as expected. Affects `defaultSize`,
`minSize`, `maxSize`, `collapsedSize` on `<Panel>`. Confirmed in `react-resizable-panels@4.11.0`.

availableCommands.name: tool-silently-checks-zero-files
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose a linter/formatter/checker that exits 0 having processed nothing,
because the directory you ran it in matches its own ignore patterns. Use when:
(1) `biome check .` prints "Checked 0 files" and "No files were processed in
the specified paths" but exits 0, (2) `yarn lint` passes instantly in a git
worktree while the same command finds errors in the main checkout, (3) you are
running quality gates inside a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`,
`.git/worktrees/`, `.direnv/`, `node_modules/`, `.cache/` or any dot-directory
the tool's config excludes, (4) eslint reports "0 problems" with
`--no-ignore` behaving differently, (5) a CI gate is green locally but fails
on the runner. Root cause: the tool matches ignore globs like `**/.claude`
against the ABSOLUTE path, so a checkout nested under an ignored ancestor
excludes itself entirely. Fix: pass an explicit subpath, or relocate the
worktree.

availableCommands.name: typescript-optional-chain-narrowing
availableCommands.description:
TypeScript fails to narrow a possibly-undefined value out of the else/false branch
when the ternary condition uses optional chaining (?.length, ?.property, etc.).
Use when: (1) TypeScript error "X is possibly 'undefined'" appears inside the else/false
branch of a ternary that checks `!x?.length`, (2) local `tsc --noEmit` passes but a
stricter CI build fails with TS18048, (3) code pattern is `!arr?.length ? <empty> : arr.map(...)`.
Solution: flip the condition — check `arr?.length ? <list> : !isLoading ? <empty> : null`
so the truthy branch provably narrows arr to a non-empty array.

availableCommands.name: backstage-nfs-page-extension-silently-unrouted
availableCommands.description:
Two silent PageBlueprint misconfigurations in Backstage's New Frontend
System that make a plugin page unreachable or invisible with nothing logged.
Use when: (1) a `createFrontendPlugin` page 404s ("ERROR 404: PAGE NOT
FOUND" / "Looks like someone dropped the mic!") at every URL including its
own root, while the plugin's entity tab and APIs work fine, (2) a plugin
page is reachable by URL but never appears in the sidebar while Catalog and
Search do, (3) you set `title` on PageBlueprint expecting a nav item and got
none, (4) your route path ends in `/*` because the page's own sub-paths
contain slashes. Root causes: the app router appends its own splat, so a
trailing wildcard in `params.path` nests a splat inside a splat and matches
nothing; and nav items are auto-discovered from page extensions that carry
ALL THREE of `title`, `icon` and `routeRef`. Neither failure logs anything.

availableCommands.name: grep-cannot-answer-callgraph-questions
availableCommands.description:
Three review claims LOOK like text-search questions but are dataflow/call-graph
questions, and grep answers all three wrongly: "this code is dead", "this directory
is free of inline handlers/javascript: hrefs", and "this output is unescaped".
Use when reviewing a refactor in a codebase with shared view helpers or sanitize-
the-whole-row functions, before deleting code as dead, before accepting a
"zero occurrences" cleanliness metric, or before filing an XSS finding on a raw
`echo` in a template.

availableCommands.name: nextjs-global-error-prerender-bug
availableCommands.description:
Workaround for Next.js 16.2.2 build failure caused by _global-error being
unconditionally queued for static prerendering. Use when: (1) next build
fails with "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')"
on /_global-error, (2) export const dynamic = "force-dynamic" in
global-error.tsx is ignored, (3) error occurs on both Turbopack and webpack.
Patches next/dist/build/utils.js to return appConfig: { revalidate: 0 } so
the static-path collection loop in build/index.js skips _global-error.

availableCommands.name: prisma-7-client-adapter-setup
availableCommands.description:
Set up PrismaClient in Prisma 7 using a driver adapter (required). Use when:
(1) `new PrismaClient()` throws "PrismaClient needs to be constructed with a
non-empty, valid PrismaClientOptions", (2) passing `{ datasourceUrl: ... }` throws
"Unknown property datasourceUrl", (3) upgrading from Prisma 6 to 7 and runtime
queries fail even though migrations work, (4) writing a seed script or app module
that needs the Prisma ORM client in Prisma 7. Root cause: Prisma 7 removed the
`url` field from schema.prisma and requires an explicit driver adapter
(e.g. @prisma/adapter-pg) passed to the PrismaClient constructor.

availableCommands.name: daisyui-vite8-plugin-css-resolution
availableCommands.description:
Fix for "TypeError: Unknown file extension '.css'" build error when using
@plugin "daisyui" in TailwindCSS v4 CSS files with Vite 8 (rolldown bundler).
Use when: (1) build fails with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION for
node_modules/daisyui/daisyui.css, (2) using @tailwindcss/vite 4.2.x+ with
Vite 8+, (3) also affects WXT 0.20+ (bundles Vite 8 internally). Root cause:
DaisyUI package.json has "browser": "./daisyui.css" — Vite 8's CSS resolver
picks this field and tries to ESM-import the CSS file, which Node rejects.
Fix: use @plugin "daisyui/index.js" to bypass browser field resolution.

availableCommands.name: biome-migrate-disables-recommended-rules
availableCommands.description:
Catches a silent footgun where `biome migrate --write` rewrites a Biome 2.x
config's `"rules": { "recommended": true }` into `"rules": { "preset": "none" }`,
which DISABLES ALL LINT RULES instead of preserving the recommended set. Use when:
(1) you ran `biome migrate` / `npx @biomejs/biome migrate --write` to clear a
deprecation notice about the `recommended` field, (2) after a Biome upgrade `biome
check` suddenly reports far fewer (or zero) lint findings, (3) reviewing a biome.json
diff that changed `recommended: true` to `preset: "none"` or `preset: "off"`, (4) lint
rules that used to fire stopped firing with no code change. The fix is to set
`"preset": "recommended"` (not "none"). Verify by re-running `biome check` and
confirming recommended-rule violations are reported again.

availableCommands.name: astro-mcp-rewrites-vscode-mcp-json
availableCommands.description:
Explains why `.vscode/mcp.json` keeps showing up as modified in `git status`
in an Astro project, with only the port changing (e.g. localhost:4321 ->
4322). Use when: (1) `.vscode/mcp.json` is dirty in a worktree you never
edited that file in, (2) the diff is a single line changing the `__mcp/sse`
URL's port, (3) the file goes dirty again immediately after you `git checkout`
it, (4) you are about to commit it, "preserve" it as a user preference, or
copy it between worktrees, (5) two worktrees running dev servers on different
ports keep fighting over it. Root cause: the `astro-mcp` integration rewrites
the file to whatever port `astro dev` bound, so it is a GENERATED artifact
keyed to a transient port, not a human edit. Treat it as build output:
revert before committing, or gitignore it.

availableCommands.name: pg-view-select-star-frozen-columns
availableCommands.description:
Fix new table columns being invisible to every reader that goes through a
Postgres view defined with `SELECT *`. Use when: (1) you ran
`ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c ...`, the column exists in `\d t`, but queries
against a view over `t` error with `column "c" does not exist` or silently
return no such field, (2) an ORM/app layer that reads exclusively through a
view cannot see a column you just migrated in, (3) `\d+ v` shows an older
column list than `\d t`, (4) a migration adding a column passed every test
and shipped columns nothing could read, (5) same symptom for a TimescaleDB
hypertable read through a filtered guard view. Root cause: Postgres expands
`SELECT *` to a fixed column list AT VIEW-CREATION TIME and stores the
resolved list in the rewrite rule — the star is not re-evaluated on read, so
the view keeps its original shape forever. Fix: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` in
the same migration that adds the column.

availableCommands.name: nextjs-ppr-connection-opt-out
availableCommands.description:
Fix for Prisma/database errors during Next.js build with cacheComponents (PPR) enabled.
Symptom: "prisma:error Invalid prisma.X.findMany() invocation" printed during
"Generating static pages" phase, even though the page is marked ◐ (Partial Prerender).
Caused by pages that do direct DB calls but have no dynamic API (cookies/headers/searchParams),
so PPR attempts to pre-render them statically. Fix: add `await connection()` from 'next/server'.

availableCommands.name: node-ipv6-fetch-ehostunreach
availableCommands.description:
Fix intermittent "fetch failed" / connect EHOSTUNREACH errors when Node
server code fetches external hosts (Google Fonts, APIs) on networks with
broken IPv6. Use when: (1) an Astro/Next/Vite dev server or build
intermittently throws TypeError: fetch failed with cause EHOSTUNREACH on a
2607:/2a00:-style IPv6 address or ETIMEDOUT, (2) the same URL works
instantly with curl, (3) failures are flaky — some renders succeed, others
error (e.g. astro-google-fonts-optimizer fetching per SSR render). Fix:
NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first.

availableCommands.name: rsc-payload-dollar-markers-are-not-money
availableCommands.description:
Stop misreading a React Server Components (Next.js App Router) streamed payload
when verifying rendered values by scraping HTML. Use when: (1) you curl a Next
App Router page and the visible text is only the nav/shell because the content
streams inside `self.__next_f.push([1,"..."])` scripts, (2) you grep the HTML
for `\$[0-9]` to check a currency figure and get plausible-but-wrong numbers
like `$202`, `$L1`, `$206`, (3) two pages return nearly identical byte counts
and you suspect one shell rather than two dashboards, (4) you are verifying
that a UI renders real values rather than an em dash or `$0.00`. Root cause:
in the RSC wire format a leading `$` is a REFERENCE MARKER (`"$L2"` lazy,
`"$202"` row ref, `"$undefined"`), not a dollar sign — so a currency regex
matches serialization internals. Fix: render the page in a real browser and
read it, rather than text-scraping the payload.

availableCommands.name: vitest-mock-factory-hoisted-refs
availableCommands.description:
Fix "Cannot access 'X' before initialization" / TDZ errors or undefined
mock variables when a Vitest `vi.mock()` factory references a variable
defined outside the mock. Use when: (1) `vi.mock("@/module", () => ({ fn: () => someVar }))`
where `someVar = vi.fn()` is declared at top-level, (2) the test file throws
ReferenceError at import time, (3) the mock factory returns a function that
references an outer `sendMail`, `rateCheck`, `handler`, or similar vi.fn().
Vitest hoists `vi.mock()` calls above ALL imports and module-level code,
so any variable the factory closes over must also be hoisted via `vi.hoisted()`.

availableCommands.name: preview-fill-react-controlled-input-noop
availableCommands.description:
Explains why filling a React controlled input via a browser-automation/preview MCP
(e.g. Claude_Preview `preview_fill`, or a raw `input.value = x` + dispatched event) can
leave the component's state EMPTY even though the input visibly shows the typed text —
so a subsequent "submit" button silently no-ops and nothing persists. Use when:
(1) driving a React app through preview_fill / preview_click and a form submit appears
to do nothing, (2) the text is visible in the field but the app behaves as if the field
is empty (handler early-returns on a blank value), (3) only SOME forms work while others
silently fail, (4) you need to decide whether a "write didn't persist" finding is a real
app bug or an automation artifact. Root cause: the fill bypasses React's value tracker so
`onChange` never fires and controlled state stays stale; React then skips reconciling the
DOM value back, so the field keeps showing the injected text. Resolution: verify write
paths with a jsdom `@testing-library/user-event` test (which fires genuine React events),
not with the browser preview tool; treat preview_fill as reliable only for reads/layout.

availableCommands.name: nginx-exact-location-inherits-no-root
availableCommands.description:
Nginx returns 404 for a static file that demonstrably exists in the webroot,
and nothing appears in the error log. Use when: (1) `/favicon.ico`,
`/robots.txt`, `/50x.html` or similar 404s while sibling paths under the same
server serve fine, (2) the file is confirmed present inside the container
(`docker exec ... ls /opt/www/favicon.ico` succeeds) yet the request 404s,
(3) the error log shows NO "No such file or directory" entry for the failing
request, (4) an identical-looking sibling site/image serves the same file
correctly, making it look image-specific, (5) you are reviewing a config where
an included/shared snippet declares `location = /favicon.ico { log_not_found
off; }` and `root` is declared only inside `location /`. Root cause: an
exact-match location outranks the prefix location and inherits `root` from
server/http level, not from `location /` — so with no server-level root it
resolves against nginx's compiled-in default. `nginx -t` passes, because the
config is syntactically valid.

availableCommands.name: subagent-hallucinated-commit
availableCommands.description:
Fix for subagent implementers (especially Haiku) reporting DONE status with a fabricated
commit SHA and test results, when in reality no commit was made and working-tree changes
don't exist. Use when: (1) using subagent-driven-development, (2) implementer reports
DONE with commit SHA, (3) controller verification via `git log` or `git status` shows
no new commit exists, OR the file they claimed to create/edit is missing/unchanged,
OR previously-existing files are now deleted. Prevention: always verify commit SHA
exists via `git log --oneline -1 <claimed_sha>` AND `git status` shows clean tree
BEFORE dispatching spec reviewer. Recovery: restore any accidentally deleted files
from HEAD, fix the work directly (faster) or re-dispatch with a more capable model
and explicit post-commit verification step.

availableCommands.name: improve-codebase-architecture
availableCommands.description: Find deepening opportunities in a codebase, informed by the domain language in CONTEXT.md and the decisions in docs/adr/. Use when the user wants to improve architecture, find refactoring opportunities, consolidate tightly-coupled modules, or make a codebase more testable and AI-navigable.

availableCommands.name: tsconfig-include-excludes-test-dirs
availableCommands.description:
Detect a monorepo typecheck gate that reports success while never checking
most of the test suite, because each workspace's `tsconfig.json` sets
`"include": ["src/**/*"]` while its tests live in a sibling `test/`
directory. Use when: (1) `tsc --noEmit` / `turbo run typecheck` passes but a
type error in a test file reaches review or CI unnoticed, (2) moving a test
file from `test/` into `src/` suddenly produces type errors it never had,
(3) a test uses a stale API signature and nothing complained, (4) mocks or
fixtures drift out of shape with the code they stand in for, (5) you are
about to trust "typecheck is green" as evidence the tests compile, (6) tests
co-located under `src/` are checked while a sibling `test/` directory is not,
in the same repo. Root cause: `include` is a whitelist — anything outside it
is invisible to tsc, silently and with exit 0. Detection: append a deliberate
type error to a test file and confirm typecheck FAILS; if it passes, that
directory is outside the gate.

availableCommands.name: claudeception
availableCommands.description:
Claudeception is a continuous learning system that extracts reusable knowledge from work sessions.
Triggers: (1) /claudeception command to review session learnings, (2) "save this as a skill"
or "extract a skill from this", (3) "what did we learn?", (4) After any task involving
non-obvious debugging, workarounds, or trial-and-error discovery. Creates new Claude Code
skills when valuable, reusable knowledge is identified.

availableCommands.name: coverage-config-measures-less-than-you-think
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose a code-coverage percentage that is high because most of the code was
never measured. Use when: (1) coverage reads ~85-90% but you doubt the suite
earns it, (2) a coverage `exclude` glob like `'**/index.ts'` was written for
"barrel files" in a framework where `index.ts` / `route.ts` / `page.tsx` are
actual entry points, (3) a coverage ratchet has never once failed, (4)
thresholds sit far below the reported number, (5) a comment records measured
percentages that no longer match reality, (6) upgrading to Vitest 4 and
`coverage.all` is now a TYPE ERROR (`'all' does not exist in type
'CoverageOptions'`), (7) a workspace's `tsconfig.json` includes only `["src"]`
so its own `vitest.config.ts` is never typechecked and dead config survives
invisibly.

availableCommands.name: claude-code-plugin-authoring
availableCommands.description:
Create and publish a Claude Code plugin from a GitHub repository. Use when:
(1) converting a skills collection into an installable plugin,
(2) structuring a new plugin repo from scratch,
(3) understanding how Claude Code discovers skills/commands/agents from a plugin,
(4) setting up multi-machine plugin distribution via GitHub marketplace,
(5) missing marketplace.json causing /plugin marketplace add to fail.
Covers .claude-plugin/plugin.json AND .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (BOTH required),
skills/ auto-discovery, local vs marketplace installation, and migrating from manual
~/.claude/skills symlinks.

availableCommands.name: vitest-module-mock-stale-call-count
availableCommands.description:
Vitest module-level vi.fn() mocks (created inside vi.mock() factory) retain their
call history between tests in the same file. A test asserting toNotHaveBeenCalled()
will fail if a previous test in the same describe block called that mock. Use when:
(1) `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`
for a function that logically shouldn't run in the current test, (2) tests pass in
isolation but fail when run together, (3) the failing test runs after a test that
successfully invokes the same mock. Fix: add beforeEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks()).

availableCommands.name: caddy-request-body-inline-max-size-ignored
availableCommands.description:
Catch a Caddy `request_body max_size` written inline, which adapts without
error while silently discarding the limit — and check what depends on the
limit being absent before repairing it. Use when: (1) a Caddyfile contains
`request_body max_size 10MB` on one line rather than in a block,
(2) uploads far larger than a configured max_size succeed and you cannot see
why, (3) a linter, review bot, or `caddy adapt` finding claims an inline
`request_body` "prevents Caddy from loading the config" and you need to know
whether that is true (it is not — it exits 0), (4) you are porting a
Caddy-fronted docker-compose stack to Traefik/nginx and reproducing its body
limit, (5) you are about to "fix" any silently-ignored proxy limit, timeout,
or quota. Root cause: Caddy's parseCaddyfile consumes the directive name then
reads only `h.NextBlock(0)`, so same-line tokens are never read; the emitted
JSON is a bare {"handler": "request_body"} with no max_size. The trap that
follows: an app whose per-route limits exceed the proxy's nominal cap has
been working only because the cap never applied, so writing it correctly
introduces 413s that never existed.

availableCommands.name: i18n-brand-token-interpolation
availableCommands.description:
Pattern for centralizing brand name (and other globally-constant tokens) inside next-intl
message JSON without touching every t() call site. Use when: (1) brand name / domain /
support email is hardcoded in messages/en.json / messages/es.json across many keys,
(2) you want an env-var-overridable brand for whitelabel, (3) refactoring every
useTranslations/getTranslations call site to pass values is impractical. Solution:
scoped token substitution (`{brand}`, `{supportEmail}`) applied once at message-load
time in i18n/request.ts, before next-intl sees the messages.

availableCommands.name: biome-autofix-blocked-by-errors
availableCommands.description:
Fix workflow when biome check --write reports "Some errors were emitted while applying
fixes" and exits 1 without applying any fixes, even for unrelated warnings. Use when:
(1) bun run check (biome check --write) silently skips all fixes, (2) biome reports
"No fixes applied" alongside warnings that should be auto-fixable, (3) errors and
fixable warnings are in different files but fixes still don't apply.

availableCommands.name: dag-executor-succeeded-vs-finished-sets
availableCommands.description:
Fix infinite loop or duplicate-task-execution bugs in dependency-graph
executors (CI runners, workflow orchestrators, build systems, Temporal
fan-out workflows) where one set tracks both "task is done" AND "dependents
may now run". Use when: (1) tasks that return FAILED/TIMED_OUT get
re-picked every loop iteration, (2) DAG runner appears to hang on a single
failed node and keeps re-spawning it, (3) executor throws
WorkflowExecutionAlreadyStartedError / "task X already running" / similar
on retry of a known-failed task, (4) loop-termination condition uses the
same set as dependency-satisfaction check (e.g. `completedRepos`,
`doneNodes`, `processedSteps`), (5) reviewing dep-graph executor code and
spotting one Set used for both gates. Root cause: "satisfies dependents"
(only SUCCESS counts) and "is finished" (any terminal verdict counts) are
different invariants — collapsing them into one Set means failed tasks
never advance the finished count, so the runnable filter keeps picking
them, and the start-task call throws because the underlying handle/job
already exists.

availableCommands.name: compose-environment-shadows-env-file
availableCommands.description:
A key listed in a Compose service's `environment:` SILENTLY WINS over the same
key in its `env_file:`, so a secret you carefully moved into an env file is
ignored and the container gets whatever `${VAR:-}` resolved to — usually empty.
Use when: (1) a value you put in .env.secrets / env_file has no effect and the
app behaves as if it were unset, (2) you added a documented "slot" for a
credential in an example env file and it never took, (3) a token-bearing URL
or password reads empty in the container but is plainly present in the file,
(4) you are moving a secret OUT of a tracked .env into a gitignored env file
and need to know what else must change, (5) you are about to verify what a
container receives and are reaching for `docker compose config`. Covers the
precedence rule, why `docker compose config` is a reliable oracle for this
but NOT for `$`-bearing values under `format: raw`, and reading the variable
inside the container as the check that cannot lie.

availableCommands.name: riot-component-testing-jsdom-esm
availableCommands.description:
Set up mocha + jsdom to unit-test Riot.js `.riot` single-file components in an
ESM project ("type": "module"). Use when: (1) the test suite can only import
plain modules and `.riot` components are untestable, (2) importing a `.riot`
file fails with `Unknown file extension ".riot"` or the raw template text is
parsed as JS, (3) `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for an extensionless import such as
`../../scripts/utils` that rollup resolves happily, (4) `TypeError: Cannot set
property navigator of #<Object> which has only a getter` on Node 22+ when
installing jsdom globals, (5) a `.riot` `<style>` block written in scss breaks
the test run. Provides a Node module customization hook that compiles `.riot`
on import, plus the jsdom global setup.

availableCommands.name: intl-supportedvaluesof-not-a-validator
availableCommands.description:
Fixes false "Invalid timezone" / "Invalid currency" / "Invalid calendar"
rejections caused by using `Intl.supportedValuesOf(...)` as a membership
validator. Use when: (1) a user enters "UTC", "GMT", "EST", "US/Eastern" or
"Etc/UTC" in a timezone field and gets a 400 / validation error, (2) code
contains `new Set(Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')).has(x)` or
`.includes(x)` as an input check, (3) a timezone that works fine in
`Intl.DateTimeFormat` / `toLocaleString` / Luxon / date-fns-tz is rejected by
your own validator, (4) a profile/settings save silently clears or loudly
refuses a legitimate IANA zone, (5) tests pin a real zone like 'EST' as a
"typo" case. Root cause: `supportedValuesOf` enumerates CANONICAL identifiers
only and deliberately omits UTC and every legacy Link alias. The correct
check is a try/catch around `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

availableCommands.name: mariadb-max-statement-time-kills-writes
availableCommands.description:
MariaDB's max_statement_time aborts UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT, not just SELECT —
unlike MySQL's max_execution_time — so adding a "query timeout" from
MySQL-oriented advice silently breaks long maintenance writes. Use when:
(1) adding max_statement_time to a MariaDB server to stop runaway queries or
make an overloaded DB self-heal, (2) a batch/migration/cron .sql job started
failing partway after a DB config change, (3) mysql batch mode aborts mid-file
with ER_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT / "Query execution was interrupted (max_statement_time
exceeded)", (4) a nightly data-rewrite job stops applying later statements with
no other error, (5) you are porting my.cnf tuning between MySQL and MariaDB,
(6) you need to exempt one job from a global statement timeout, (7) you are
auditing which jobs need exemptions and are about to assume the nightly
mysqldump/mariadb-dump is one of them. Covers the SET SESSION and
SET STATEMENT ... FOR exemptions, why per-statement budgets mislead, and why
mariadb-dump needs no exemption at all.

availableCommands.name: frontend-design
availableCommands.description: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, artifacts, posters, or applications (examples include websites, landing pages, dashboards, React components, HTML/CSS layouts, or when styling/beautifying any web UI). Generates creative, polished code and UI design that avoids generic AI aesthetics.

availableCommands.name: to-prd
availableCommands.description: Turn the current conversation context into a PRD and publish it to the project issue tracker. Use when user wants to create a PRD from the current context.

availableCommands.name: fastify-response-schema-strips-payload
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose a Fastify route that returns `{}` or silently drops fields from an
otherwise correct handler. Use when: (1) an endpoint returns an empty object
`{}` while the handler demonstrably returns data, (2) a response is missing
properties the handler definitely set (a chart renders empty, a badge is
blank, a client reads `undefined`), (3) an error response arrives as `{}` so
the client falls back to `statusText` instead of the server's `message`,
(4) a frontend crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined" on a field
of a truthy-but-empty API response, (5) you are reviewing a route whose
`schema.response[200]` is written as a bare `{ type: 'object' }`. Root cause:
`schema.response` is a SERIALIZER (fast-json-stringify), not documentation —
it emits only declared properties and defaults `additionalProperties` to
false. Nothing throws, nothing logs, no test fails.

availableCommands.name: svg-chart-density-viewbox-not-pixels
availableCommands.description:
A computed "pick the right granularity/bucketing for the space" default in a
React SVG chart silently never takes effect, or takes effect at the wrong size.
Use when: (1) you added auto-bucketing (day/week/month, LOD, decimation) and the
chart still renders at the finest level, (2) the auto-default works on a wide
screen but a narrow/mobile viewport still crams every point in, (3) you sized a
density decision by dividing a fixed `viewBox` width (e.g. CHART_W) by a
min-pixels-per-point constant, (4) you passed a computed default into a hook like
useHashParam/useQueryParam/useLocalStorage and it froze at first paint, (5) a
toggle "overrides" the default but the default never reappears, (6) your density
threshold passes by a hair and dots still overlap. Two independent root causes:
viewBox units are NOT CSS pixels under width:100%, and a hook that captures its
fallback via useState(read) captures it exactly once.

availableCommands.name: ai-sdk-v6-embedding-provider-options
availableCommands.description:
Fix Vercel AI SDK v6 build break: `provider.embedding(modelId, opts)` no
longer accepts a second settings argument. Use when: (1) upgrading `ai`
from v4/v5 → v6 or `@ai-sdk/openai` from 1.x/2.x → 3.x and TypeScript
reports `error TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 2.` on a line like
`createOpenAI(...).embedding(modelId, { dimensions: 1536 })`,
(2) calls to `.textEmbeddingModel(id, opts)` on
`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` similarly fail, (3) you need to forward
per-call provider settings (dimensions, encoding format, user, etc.)
with the new SDK. Root cause: AI SDK v6 split provider settings out of
the model factory; per-invocation options now flow through
`providerOptions` on `embed()` / `embedMany()`. The model factory now
takes only the model id and returns an `EmbeddingModelV3`.

availableCommands.name: gitlab-runner-system-failure-not-your-code
availableCommands.description:
A red GitLab pipeline whose job log ends in "ERROR: Job failed (system failure)"
— typically "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
during "Preparing the docker executor" — is a RUNNER infrastructure fault, not a
code failure. Use when: (1) a job fails with no test/lint/build output at all,
(2) the log shows repeated "Preparation failed" / "Will be retried in 3s",
(3) a pipeline goes red immediately after a push that changed nothing relevant,
(4) downstream `needs:`-gated jobs all show "skipped",
(5) the log ends in a DNS timeout pulling the runner helper image —
"dial tcp: lookup registry.gitlab.com on 127.0.0.53:53: i/o timeout" —
classified `runner_external_dependency_failure`,
(6) you added a `retry` policy and the job STILL fails, because every attempt
landed on the same broken runner. Covers how to confirm it, how to retry only
the affected job (not the whole pipeline), how to make GitLab self-heal these,
and why a fast-failing runner monopolises the queue so retries cannot escape
it.

availableCommands.name: metadata-action-tag-event-filtering
availableCommands.description:
Fix missing Docker image tags when using docker/metadata-action with an explicit tags: block.
Use when: (1) pushing a v* git tag but the version tag (v1.2.3) never appears in GHCR/registry,
(2) branch name tag missing on push events, (3) pr-N tag not appearing on pull_request events,
(4) `enable=${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}` looks wrong but works,
(5) confused about why {{is_default_branch}} and ${{ }} look similar but behave differently.
Covers: explicit tags block suppressing metadata-action defaults, event-type filtering per
type=ref entry, and the GHA pre-interpolation vs metadata-action bake template distinction.

availableCommands.name: rtl-findby-already-present-no-wait
availableCommands.description:
A React Testing Library `await findBy*` provides ZERO synchronisation when the
element it queries is already in the DOM — findBy = getBy + waitFor, so it
resolves on its first poll and waits for nothing. The test then races. Use when:
(1) a test is intermittently flaky with `toHaveBeenLastCalledWith` / `toHaveBeenCalledWith`
receiving the value from BEFORE the action under test, (2) the flaky assertion sits
after a second `await screen.findBy...` for an element an earlier findBy in the same
test already resolved, (3) a test asserting on a re-render, refetch, prop change or
state change passes ~95% of the time and fails rarely in CI, (4) the "wait" looks
present in the code so the race is invisible on inspection. Fix: await the condition
being asserted — `await waitFor(() => expect(mock).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(...))` —
not an element that already exists.

availableCommands.name: riot-template-scope-not-module-scope
availableCommands.description:
Fix a Riot.js (.riot SFC) template expression that renders nothing while the
build stays green. Use when: (1) a value imported at the top of a `.riot` file
and used in `{ … }` renders as empty/undefined, (2) an `if="{ someImport }"`
block never appears even though the value is definitely non-empty, (3) a
constant declared with `const` in the `<script>` block but outside
`export default` is invisible to the template, (4) you grep the built bundle
for a string you expect to be inlined and it is absent entirely, (5) a value
that works in a lifecycle method like `onMounted` is undefined in the markup.
Root cause: the Riot compiler emits template expressions as
`evaluate: (scope) => scope.name`, resolving against the COMPONENT INSTANCE,
not the module closure — so a module-scope binding reads as `undefined`, and
tree-shaking then drops the now-unused import so the value never reaches the
bundle. Fix: also expose it as a property on the `export default` object.

availableCommands.name: annotate-strips-class-docs
availableCommands.description:
annotate_models (gem) deletes hand-written class-level documentation comments

Solution: move docs INSIDE the class body, or set skip_on_db_migrate=true in .annotate_models.

availableCommands.name: loki-wal-disk-full-ingester-readonly
availableCommands.description:
Grafana Loki rejects every log push with HTTP 500 "Ingester is shutting down"
when the filesystem holding its WAL crosses 90% full — while the container stays
up, restarts cleanly, and /ready keeps answering "ready". Use when: (1) pushes to
/loki/api/v1/push return 500 with `rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Ingester is
shutting down`, (2) Promtail/Alloy/Fluent Bit log `final error sending batch` with
status 500 against a Loki that looks healthy, (3) Loki accepted logs yesterday and
refuses today with no config change, (4) `docker compose ps` shows Up and healthy
but Grafana shows no new lines, (5) you see `msg="disk usage exceeded threshold,
throttling writes" component=wal` in Loki's logs. Root cause is the ingester WAL
guard `ingester.wal.disk_full_threshold` (default 0.9) flipping the ingester
read-only; the error names the ingester and never mentions disk space.

availableCommands.name: threejs-cel-outline-lowpoly-faceting
availableCommands.description:
Fix for a low-poly mesh rendering covered in internal dark edges — looking
faceted, "crystalline," or like the wrong material — under a Three.js
screen-space cel/toon outline (pmndrs `postprocessing` NormalPass + a custom
normal-discontinuity edge Effect, or OutlineEffect). Use when: (1) a smooth
decorative object (cloud, rock, gem, sphere, capsule) shows hard edges ALL OVER
its surface, not just its silhouette, (2) a soft white cloud reads as a faceted
grey rock, (3) you recently added a screen-space normal-based outline. Root
cause: coarse geometry's per-facet normal steps exceed the outline's
normal-edge threshold, so the edge pass draws every facet boundary. Fix:
increase tessellation (segments) so per-facet normal steps fall below the
threshold, or raise the threshold.

availableCommands.name: rails-bundle-path-bootsnap-load-error
availableCommands.description:
Fix "cannot load such file -- bootsnap/setup (LoadError)" from config/boot.rb
when running bin/rails in CI. Use when: (1) a CI job sets BUNDLE_PATH (e.g.
vendor/bundle, often for gem caching) and then runs `bin/rails ...` directly,
(2) bundle install succeeds but `bin/rails`/`rake` crashes at config/boot.rb
with a LoadError for bootsnap (or any gem) even though it's in the Gemfile,
(3) the same command works in Docker/locally but not in the CI job. Root
cause: Rails' config/boot.rb requires 'bootsnap/setup' BEFORE 'bundler/setup',
so a gem relocated by BUNDLE_PATH isn't on $LOAD_PATH yet. Fix: run through
`bundle exec`.

availableCommands.name: grill-with-docs
availableCommands.description: Grilling session that challenges your plan against the existing domain model, sharpens terminology, and updates documentation (CONTEXT.md, ADRs) inline as decisions crystallise. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan against their project's language and documented decisions.

availableCommands.name: git-worktree-rebase-state-path
availableCommands.description:
Fix scripts that check `.git/rebase-merge` (or `.git/MERGE_HEAD`,
`.git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `.git/rebase-apply`) and behave wrongly inside a
git worktree. Use when: (1) a loop that should resolve rebase conflicts
exits immediately claiming "rebase complete" while `git status` still shows
`interactive rebase in progress` and unmerged paths, (2) `ls .git/rebase-*`
returns "no matches found" but a rebase is clearly running, (3) automation
around `git rebase --continue` / `git merge` / `git cherry-pick` works in a
normal clone but silently no-ops in a worktree, (4) `.git` is a FILE
containing `gitdir: ...` rather than a directory. Root cause: a linked
worktree's per-worktree state lives under
`<main-repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>/`, not `.git/`. Always resolve it with
`git rev-parse --git-dir`.

availableCommands.name: graphql-ruby-unwrap-strips-list-wrapper
availableCommands.description:
graphql-ruby `Type#unwrap` strips BOTH NonNull AND List wrappers, returning the
innermost named type. Use when: (1) writing introspection code that maps GraphQL
argument/field types to JSON schema (or any type metadata) and a `when 'LIST'`
branch on `type.unwrap.kind.name` never fires, (2) a list-typed arg like `[ID!]!`
silently maps to the scalar's mapping (e.g. `{type:'string'}`) instead of
`{type:'array'}`, (3) you need to detect list-ness or nullability of a wrapped
GraphQL type. Fix: ask wrapper-shape questions (`type.list?`, `type.non_null?`)
on the UN-unwrapped type BEFORE calling `unwrap`; `list?` sees through an outer
NonNull.

availableCommands.name: git-worktree-remove-discards-staged-work
availableCommands.description:
Fix or recover from `git worktree remove` destroying work that was written (and
even `git add`-ed) inside a worktree, while the branch survives pointing at its
base commit. Use when: (1) an agent/CI pipeline farmed work out to a worktree,
cleanup ran, and the "kept" branch turns out to be empty, (2) `git log
<branch>` shows zero commits after base though the tool reported success,
(3) `git worktree remove --force` was run and files are now gone, (4) you are
writing an orchestrator that creates a worktree, has something write into it,
then cleans up, (5) `git ls-tree -r <branch>` does not list files you watched
get created. Key insight: `git add` is NOT persistence — a worktree's index
lives in .git/worktrees/<name>/index and is deleted with the worktree, so only
a real commit survives cleanup. Includes recovery via `git fsck --lost-found`,
which still finds the blobs until GC runs.

availableCommands.name: factorybot-computed-nil-guard
availableCommands.description:
Fix FactoryBot factory crashes with NoMethodError or TypeError when tests pass nil
for fields that other lazy-evaluated factory attributes depend on. Use when:
(1) build(:model, field_a: nil) crashes with "undefined method '+' for nil",
(2) A factory attribute is computed from other factory attributes (e.g., next_km
derived from last_km + maintenance_interval), (3) Tests intentionally nil one
of the dependency fields to test presence validations. Fix: add nil guard in the
lazy block using the && ternary pattern.

availableCommands.name: build-inlined-public-env-missing-in-ci
availableCommands.description:
Fix a feature that works locally but silently breaks in a CI-built deploy
because a build-time-inlined public env var (`PUBLIC_*` in Astro,
`VITE_*` in Vite, `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` in Next.js) was only ever set in an
untracked local `.env`. Use when: (1) a form/widget posts to the wrong
URL or a relative path in production but works from a local `yarn deploy`
/ `npm run deploy`, (2) `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_X ?? ''` or
`process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_X || ''` resolves empty only in CI builds,
(3) you are porting a local deploy script to GitHub Actions / GitLab CI
and the repo has a gitignored `.env`, (4) CI is green, the build succeeds,
and the bug only appears at runtime in the browser, (5) an API base URL,
analytics key, or feature flag is undefined in a deployed bundle.
Root cause: these vars are statically inlined into the artifact at BUILD
time, so a var absent from the CI environment is baked in as the fallback
value — producing a successful build that is silently misconfigured.
Fix: set the var in CI AND assert it landed in the built output.

availableCommands.name: syslog-ng-elasticsearch-http-timestamp-key
availableCommands.description:
syslog-ng's elasticsearch-http() SCL emits "@timestamp" but SigLens (and other backends)
expect a differently-named timestamp key, so events ingest with HTTP 200 / status 201 yet
carry ingest time instead of event time. Use when: (1) shipping syslog-ng to SigLens,
Elasticsearch, OpenSearch or a Splunk-HEC-compatible store via elasticsearch-http(),
(2) `syslog-ng-ctl stats` shows written climbing and dropped=0 but a recent-time search
returns few or no records, (3) bulk ingest replies {"errors":false,...,"status":201} yet
the data is not where you expect on the timeline, (4) all events appear clustered at the
moment of ingestion rather than spread over their real times, (5) you need to configure
index(), template() or disk-buffer() on a syslog-ng HTTP/Elasticsearch destination.
Covers verifying ingest by querying data back rather than trusting the 2xx.

availableCommands.name: docker-bind-mount-uid-macos-hides-linux-failure
availableCommands.description:
A container running as a non-root UID cannot write to a bind mount Docker just
created, but the bug is INVISIBLE on macOS because Docker Desktop remaps
ownership — so it ships green and fails on the Linux host. Use when: (1) a
container dies at startup with "permission denied" creating a directory under a
bind-mounted volume, (2) a compose stack works on your Mac and crash-loops on a
Linux server with no config difference, (3) the image declares a non-root User
(Loki 10001, Grafana 472, Prometheus 65534, Elasticsearch 1000) and mounts
./data, (4) you need to verify a bind-mount permission fix but only have macOS,
(5) you are writing a setup script that must chown a data dir without sudo, (6)
`stat` inside the container reports uid 0 on macOS yet writes succeed, making a
UID comparison the wrong check. Covers reproducing the Linux failure from macOS
using an unshared VM path, probing writability instead of ownership, and
chowning from a root container rather than with sudo.

(4) a shell loop over discussion IDs silently runs once with all IDs concatenated

real comments from system events, and the position fields that locate inline diff
comments.

Use when: (1) reskinning a legacy CMS/admin (Joomla, WordPress, Drupal, Mambo, phpBB, old Rails) whose PHP/templates hardcode across dozens of files, (2) you want crisp, currentColor-themeable icons that inherit hover/dark-mode colors, (3) you must avoid touching server templates for risk/scope reasons. Covers the 0x0-content-box bitmap-hiding trick, the end-anchored-with-leading-slash selector to avoid substring collisions (publish vs unpublish), and semantic-colored status icons via background-color.

availableCommands.name: zsh-noclobber-silently-skips-file-overwrite
availableCommands.description:
Catch a file rewrite that never happened because zsh's `noclobber` option
refused to truncate an existing file. Use when: (1) `cat > file <<'EOF'`
heredoc appears to run but the file still holds the OLD content,
(2) a shell line prints `zsh: file exists: <name>` or
`(eval):NN: file exists: <name>` yet the surrounding `&&` chain seems to keep
going, (3) you rewrote a config/compose/source file via shell redirection and
a later validation still reflects the previous version, (4) an agent-authored
file edit "succeeded" with no error surfaced but the change is absent,
(5) `echo x > existing.txt` fails while `echo x > new.txt` works. Root cause:
with `setopt noclobber`, plain `>` on an EXISTING file is an error, not a
truncate; first-time creates succeed, so the failure only appears on rewrites.
Fix: use `>|` (or `>!`), or write via a dedicated file-write tool, and always
verify the file's new first line.

availableCommands.name: biome-ansi-regex-control-char
availableCommands.description:
Fix for biome noControlCharactersInRegex error caused by ANSI escape codes in regex
literals. Use when: (1) biome flags noControlCharactersInRegex but grep shows no \x1b
in the file, (2) a regex that stripped ANSI escape codes was formatted by biome's
auto-formatter, (3) the error is at the exact column of a regex escape sequence.
Root cause: biome's formatter converts \x1b in regex literals to the literal ESC byte
(0x1B), which then triggers noControlCharactersInRegex on subsequent runs. The byte
is invisible to grep and appears as \x1b in Read/cat output but is actually a raw byte.

availableCommands.name: fastify-handler-clamp-behind-schema-is-dead
availableCommands.description:
Catches unreachable "defense-in-depth" sanitization in Fastify route handlers
that sits behind a schema constraint AJV already enforces. Use when:
(1) a handler does `x.slice(0, N)`, `Math.min(x, MAX)`, `arr.slice(0, N)` or a
trim/clamp on a body/query field whose TypeBox/JSON schema already declares
`maxLength` / `maximum` / `maxItems`, (2) a code review claims a "server-side
belt" or "clamp so a client cannot hard-fail the route", (3) coverage reports
an uncovered branch inside a handler you believe is protective, (4) you are
deciding whether a schema constraint or a handler clamp should own a limit,
(5) a comment asserts the handler tolerates oversized input but the route
actually 400s with FST_ERR_VALIDATION. Root cause: Fastify runs AJV body/query
validation BEFORE the handler, so the handler can never observe a value that
violates the schema — the clamp is dead code and the comment is false.

availableCommands.name: subagent-worktree-branch-verification
availableCommands.description:
Fix for subagent implementers committing to the wrong git branch (main instead of
feature branch) when dispatched to work in a git worktree. Use when: (1) using
subagent-driven-development with a git worktree, (2) spec reviewer reports "commit
exists but on wrong branch", (3) after task 1 completes, git log on the feature branch

in the implementer prompt. Recovery: run `git rebase main` from inside the worktree.

availableCommands.name: nodemailer-sendmail-accepted-vs-delivered
availableCommands.description:
Fix false-positive "email sent" messages in nodemailer-based test/diagnostic endpoints.
Use when: (1) `transport.sendMail(...)` resolves successfully but the recipient never
receives the message, (2) an admin "Send test email" button reports success but the
inbox is empty, (3) audit log shows `durationMs` with no error but delivery failed,
(4) building or hardening any SMTP test / diagnostic / health-check endpoint,
(5) messages vanish after being sent through SendGrid / Mailgun / SES / Postmark /
Brevo / Gmail SMTP. Root cause: `sendMail` resolves on SMTP 2xx at submission
(relay accepted) — NOT on delivery. The returned `info` object has `accepted`,
`rejected`, `response`, and `messageId` fields that MUST be inspected to distinguish
true success from silent recipient-rejection, and from provider-side spam / bounce /
unverified-sender filtering that happens after the handoff.

availableCommands.name: cpu-thermal-throttling-masquerades-as-load
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose a Linux server reported as "overloaded", "slow", or "saturated" when the
real cause is hardware CPU thermal throttling. Use when: (1) load average is many
times the core count but %wa/iowait is 0 and there is free RAM, (2) trivial work
takes absurdly long — a query on a 500-row table taking 28s, a cached homepage
taking 90s, (3) an app tier looks like it is "using a full core" under low traffic,
(4) the box crashed or hung with no OOM and no clean shutdown, (5) a previous
performance investigation refuted all its software hypotheses and stalled,
(6) the machine is fast for ~10 minutes after a cold boot then collapses.
The decisive check is scaling_cur_freq reading BELOW scaling_min_freq, which the
cpufreq governor cannot cause. Also covers dating the onset from atop history and
the ps process-vs-thread run-queue trap.

availableCommands.name: phpstan-baseline-reorder-false-positive
availableCommands.description:

and deciding whether a policy of "never baseline a new finding" was violated,
(2) a diff shows added entries but the file's total shrank, (3) adds and removes do not
reconcile against the net line change. Applies to any generated file with unstable
ordering (lockfiles, snapshot suites, codegen output).

availableCommands.name: prebuilt-nextjs-image-origin-relative-api
availableCommands.description:
Diagnose a self-hosted third-party Next.js app whose published Docker image
ignores NEXT_PUBLIC_* set at runtime, and work out the deployment topology it
actually requires. Use when: (1) you are writing docker-compose for someone
else's Next.js frontend + separate API backend (analytics dashboards, admin
panels, self-hosted SaaS) from images like ghcr.io/<vendor>/<app>-client,
(2) the dashboard HTML loads but every API call 404s or hits the frontend
container instead of the backend, (3) setting NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL /
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL in `environment:` has no effect on the browser bundle,
(4) you are deciding whether a dev overlay can publish frontend and backend
on two separate ports, (5) an upstream compose file ships BOTH `image:` and
`build:` plus a bundled Caddy/nginx and you want to drop the proxy,
(6) you need to know what a published image baked into a build-time constant
WITHOUT pulling or running it. Root cause: NEXT_PUBLIC_* and next.config
`env:` values are inlined by webpack DefinePlugin at BUILD time; a vendor CI
that builds with no build-args bakes an empty string, which makes the client
call the API relative to its own origin — so the app only works when one
hostname serves both, and a split-port setup makes the dashboard call itself.

availableCommands.name: changesets-yarn-berry-ignores-node-auth-token
availableCommands.description:
npm publish fails to authenticate in GitHub Actions despite the standard
`actions/setup-node` + `registry-url` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` recipe, because
changesets publishes a Yarn Berry workspace with `yarn npm publish`, and Yarn
reads its own config — not .npmrc. Use when: (1) `changeset publish` 401s or
404s in CI with a token that works locally, (2) you followed GitHub's
documented npm-auth-in-Actions setup and it appears to do nothing, (3) you are
wiring changesets releases in a Yarn 2/3/4 monorepo, (4) you need to know
which component performs npm OIDC trusted publishing in that stack. Fix: pass
the token as YARN_NPM_AUTH_TOKEN, or use trusted publishing (Yarn does the
OIDC exchange itself from 4.9.0).

availableCommands.name: bun-serve-sse-idle-timeout
availableCommands.description:
Fix `net::ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING 200 (OK)` on Server-Sent Events (SSE) endpoints
served by `Bun.serve()`. Use when: (1) browser DevTools shows `ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING`
on a `text/event-stream` GET that previously responded `200 OK`, (2) the SSE connection works
for a few seconds then dies, (3) heartbeats / keepalives are configured at 15-30s but the
connection still drops, (4) using Bun + Hono (or raw `Bun.serve`) for SSE, (5) symptom only
appears under load or after the first idle gap, (6) switching to Hono's `streamSSE` helper
doesn't fix it on its own. Root cause: `Bun.serve()` defaults `idleTimeout` to **10 seconds**
per request — when no bytes flow for 10s Bun tears down the socket without emitting the
chunked-encoding terminator (`0\r\n\r\n`), and the browser surfaces this as
ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING. Heartbeats slower than 10s never get a chance to fire. Fix:
set `idleTimeout` to a value above the heartbeat cadence (max 255 seconds in Bun), or drop the
heartbeat below 10s. This is a Bun runtime config issue, distinct from any app-level streaming
helper.

availableCommands.name: nextjs-catch-all-encoded-slash-segments
availableCommands.description:
Fix a Next.js App Router catch-all route ([...x]) that 404s (or mis-parses)
because a link encoded a slash with encodeURIComponent, collapsing two path
segments into one %2F segment. Use when: (1) a detail link like
/me/prs/owner%2Frepo/101 renders notFound() while the list that generated it
shows the item, (2) a [...slug] page checks params.slug.length and gets fewer
segments than expected, (3) you used encodeURIComponent(`${a}/${b}`) to build
a path, (4) navigating the same route with literal slashes (/a/b/101) works
but the encoded form (/a%2Fb/101) doesn't. Root cause: %2F inside one path
segment is decoded to a slash WITHIN that segment — it stays ONE catch-all
segment, it does NOT split into two. Fix: encode each segment separately
(`encodeURIComponent(a)/encodeURIComponent(b)/...`) so the path has real
separators and the catch-all sees the expected number of segments.

availableCommands.name: syslog-ng-scl-silently-drops-source-options
availableCommands.description:
syslog-ng's default-network-drivers() SCL silently ignores source options such as
time-zone(), so timezone-less RFC3164 messages land hours off. Use when: (1) you added
time-zone("Region/City") to default-network-drivers() and nothing changed, (2) received
BSD/RFC3164 events are stamped N hours in the past or future while arriving in real
time, (3) `syslog-ng --syntax-only` passes and the daemon starts with no warning yet an
option has no effect, (4) log events look correct in flat files but sit in the wrong
place on an indexed timeline in Loki/Elasticsearch/SigLens/OpenSearch, (5) a "last 15
minutes" search or alert never matches even though `syslog-ng-ctl stats` shows written>0
and dropped=0, (6) any option passed to an SCL block (elasticsearch-http, loki,
default-network-drivers) appears to do nothing. Root cause: the SCL forwards its
`...`/__VARARGS__ to app-parser(), NOT to the inner network() sources, so unknown
options are accepted and discarded.

availableCommands.name: prisma-7-pgvector-hnsw-migrate-dev-drift
availableCommands.description:
Fix `prisma migrate dev` always reporting drift on a pgvector HNSW (or
IVFFlat) index and prompting "Enter a name for the new migration" on every
routine setup. Use when: (1) a `db:migrate` script runs `prisma migrate
dev` and hangs at the migration-name prompt even though `prisma migrate
status` says "Database schema is up to date", (2) `prisma migrate diff
--from-config-datasource --to-schema schema.prisma` reports
`[*] Changed the agent_lessons table  [-] Removed index on columns
(embedding)` (or any vector / GiST / GIN extension index), (3) the schema
uses `embedding Unsupported("vector(1536)")?` (or similar pgvector column)
and the HNSW index is defined in raw SQL inside the init migration, (4)
Prisma 7 with `previewFeatures = ["postgresqlExtensions"]` and
`extensions = [vector]` configured. Root cause: Prisma's schema DSL has
no syntax for HNSW / IVFFlat / GIN-with-custom-ops indexes. `prisma
migrate dev` introspects the live DB on every run and compares it to the
schema; the extension-only index appears as a "removed" index in the
schema and Prisma asks you to author a new migration to "fix" it. The
loop is infinite — any new migration would just remove the index and the
next `migrate dev` would re-flag it.

availableCommands.name: biome-exit-code-driven-by-format-not-lint
availableCommands.description:
Explains why `biome check` / `npm run lint` exits 0 while still reporting
dozens of lint findings, and why that exit code is therefore not a lint gate.
Use when: (1) `biome check .` prints "Found 62 warnings" / "Found 38 infos"
and still exits 0, (2) a lint gate is green in CI while the repo carries
hundreds of unaddressed diagnostics, (3) `npm run lint` suddenly fails after

following content", (4) you are about to use an exit code to prove a
refactor/config change did not lose lint coverage, (5) you migrated
`linter.rules.recommended` and want to confirm rules still fire. Root cause:
Biome exits non-zero only on ERROR-severity diagnostics; recommended lint
rules default to warn/info, while a formatting difference is an error. Fix:
compare diagnostic COUNTS (or use --diagnostic-level / --error-on-warnings),
never the exit code alone.

availableCommands.name: rails-shared-db-parallel-test-deadlock
availableCommands.description:
Two or more `bin/rails test` runs from different git worktrees that share ONE
Postgres instance (same dev/test database names) deadlock on each other,
hanging at near-zero CPU with no output. Use when: (1) `bin/rails test` hangs
for minutes producing nothing, (2) `ps` shows multiple `ruby bin/rails test`
processes (often from sibling worktrees) all using almost no CPU, (3) a test
run aborts early with "Stopped processing SimpleCov as a previous error not
related to SimpleCov has been detected" right after "# Running:" with 0 tests,
(4) the project shares a single Dockerized Postgres across worktrees (e.g. host
port 5433). Root cause: Rails parallel test workers (>50 tests triggers
`parallelize`) from each run create/truncate the SAME `*_test`/`*_test-N`
databases and contend on DDL/advisory locks. Fix: run single-process with
`PARALLEL_WORKERS=1`, or run files in batches under the 50-test threshold, or
kill the abandoned sibling run. Also: env vars set in one Bash tool call do NOT
persist to the next — keep DB scratch scripts self-contained in one call.

availableCommands.name: guarded-ddl-cannot-converge-existing-objects
availableCommands.description:
A migration written as `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (or `ADD INDEX IF NOT
EXISTS`, `CREATE OR REPLACE`-less DDL) can ADD a missing object but can NEVER
CORRECT one that already exists — it no-ops and the environments diverge
permanently. Use when: (1) a migration that "ran successfully" left a table
with the wrong charset/collation/column default/engine, (2) production and
a schema-dump-built dev DB disagree about a table the migration was supposed
to define, (3) re-running a migration changes nothing and you are about to
conclude it was already applied, (4) you must decide whether a schema file or
the live server is authoritative, (5) a table shows `utf8mb3`/`utf8mb3_general_ci`
when every committed definition says `utf8mb4` — this fingerprints WHICH code
created it, since MySQL/MariaDB alias `CHARSET=utf8` to utf8mb3, (6) an app
lazily self-provisions a table with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` at runtime and
races the migration that also creates it, (7) a migration is HALF applied —
its ADD present, its DROP never run. Covers proving which writer won, the
ALTER-based convergence fix, and why guarded DDL makes drift silent.

availableCommands.name: zod-v4-strict-uuid-validation
availableCommands.description:
Fix unexpected zod v4 UUID validation failures after upgrading from zod v3.
Use when: (1) tests that passed in zod v3 fail with HTTP 400 / "Invalid UUID"
after `zod` 3.x → 4.x bump, (2) seemingly-valid UUIDs like
`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001` are rejected, (3) Fastify route with
`fastify-type-provider-zod` returns 400 on requests using all-zero or
fixture UUIDs, (4) error issues report
`code: "invalid_format", format: "uuid"` with a regex pattern requiring the
13th hex digit in `[1-8]` and the 17th in `[89abAB]`. Root cause: zod v4
switched `z.string().uuid()` (and the new top-level `z.uuid()`) to RFC 9562
compliance — the version nibble (1-8) and variant nibble (8/9/a/b) are now
enforced. The all-zero (nil) and all-FF (max) UUIDs are still allowed as
special cases. Affects every test fixture, seeded record, and constant that
used a "valid-looking but RFC-non-compliant" UUID.

availableCommands.name: backstage-better-sqlite3-peer-mismatch-native-crash
availableCommands.description:
A Backstage backend dies with a native V8 assertion — not a JS exception —
when the hoisted better-sqlite3 does not match the version
@backstage/backend-defaults declares as a peer. Use when: (1) the backend
prints "Assertion failed: (env) != nullptr" at
"node::RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook" with a native stack through

seconds after "Plugin initialization complete" with no JavaScript stack
trace, (3) yarn install logged two different better-sqlite3 versions being
built or rebuilt, (4) you pinned better-sqlite3 yourself in a backend
package. Root cause: two native copies in the tree, or one whose ABI
expectations differ from what backend-defaults uses; the destructor runs
during GC against a torn-down environment. Fix: pin to the peer range
backend-defaults declares.

availableCommands.name: docker-dind-workspace-transient-dns
availableCommands.description:
Fix intermittent "Could not resolve host: <host> (Timeout while contacting
DNS servers)" failures from inside Docker-in-Docker workspace/ephemeral
containers. Use when: (1) a container git clone/push/curl fails mid-job with
"Could not resolve host" even though the host and other containers resolve
fine, (2) the SAME container succeeded at an earlier network step (e.g. clone
worked, a later push failed) — i.e. the failure is transient, not persistent,
(3) the workspace container is launched with `docker run` carrying no `--dns`
flag and relies on Docker's embedded resolver (127.0.0.11), (4) running on
Docker Desktop for Mac over a flaky link (iPhone hotspot 172.20.10.x, VPN
reconnect, laptop sleep/wake). Root cause: Docker's embedded DNS forwarder
proxies to the host resolver, which briefly becomes unreachable; long-running
in-container DNS lookups then time out. Fix: pin public resolvers on the
container with `--dns=1.1.1.1 --dns=8.8.8.8`.

availableCommands.name: temporal-admin-tools-sql-password-env
availableCommands.description:
Fix `temporal-sql-tool` schema setup failing with `password authentication
failed for user "postgres"` after migrating off `temporalio/auto-setup` to
the split `temporalio/server` + `temporalio/admin-tools` topology. Use when:
(1) docker-compose has a one-shot `temporal-setup` service running
`temporalio/admin-tools` with `temporal-sql-tool create / setup-schema /
update-schema`, (2) compose passes `POSTGRES_PWD=<pw>` like the old
auto-setup did, (3) container loops on
`pq: password authentication failed for user "postgres"` followed by
`Unable to create SQL database. {"error": "no usable database connection
found"}`, (4) `psql -U postgres` works fine inside the postgres-temporal
container so the password is definitely correct, (5) the `temporal` server
container itself reaches Postgres without trouble — only the schema-setup
one-shot fails. Root cause: `temporal-sql-tool` reads its DB password from
`SQL_PASSWORD` (or the `-pw` flag), NOT `POSTGRES_PWD`. The legacy
`temporalio/auto-setup` image translated `POSTGRES_PWD` → `SQL_PASSWORD`
inside its entrypoint; standalone `temporalio/admin-tools` does not, so
the var is silently dropped and the tool connects with an empty password.

availableCommands.name: prisma-schema-type-stale-client
availableCommands.description:
