availableCommands.name: compose-env-file-dollar-interpolation
availableCommands.description:
Docker Compose interpolates the VALUES inside .env / env_file, so any secret
containing `$` is silently truncated before it ever reaches the container or a
label. Use when: (1) Traefik/nginx basic auth rejects a password you know is
correct and `htpasswd` verifies the hash locally, (2) a bcrypt/argon2 hash,
PostgreSQL URL, JWT secret or API key stored in .env arrives at the app shorter
than it went in, (3) `docker compose config` shows a value ending abruptly right
after `$$2y$$05`, (4) compose warns `The "<random-looking-string>" variable is not
set. Defaulting to a blank string.` naming a fragment of your secret, (5) the same
credential works with `docker run --env-file` but breaks under compose, (6) a
secret that worked for months breaks when rotated to a new one. Root cause: `$X`
in a .env value parses as a variable reference. Whether it corrupts depends on the
character after `$`, so ~1 in 6 bcrypt hashes survive by luck and mask the bug.
Fixes: double every `$` as `$$`, or use `env_file: [{path, format: raw}]`.

but fails when running the full suite (`bun test`), (2) a later-running test

another test file mocked via `mock.module(...)`, (3) integration tests that
shell out to a real binary suddenly behave as if the binary returned the
exact mock-default the earlier unit test set up, (4) you suspect ESM module
cache poisoning between test files, (5) an `afterAll` that re-calls
`mock.module(...)` with the real implementation has no effect because the
later test file's imports were already resolved at suite-collection time.
Root cause: Bun's `mock.module()` mutates the global module registry for
the lifetime of the `bun test` process and has no built-in restore. There
is no working `mock.restore()` for module mocks — `mock.restore()` covers
only `spyOn` mocks. Re-mocking in `afterAll` does not help because Bun
resolves every test file's top-level imports up-front before any hooks
run, so by the time `afterAll` fires, the bindings in later files are
already pointing at the stale mocks. Fix: refactor the production module
to take its side-effecty deps as an optional parameter (with sensible
default), then inject test mocks via that parameter — no `mock.module`
needed. This matches Bun's recommended pattern and is dramatically more
reliable than registry tricks.

availableCommands.name: a11y-widget-body-star-overrides-headings
availableCommands.description:

`body, body *`. Use when: (1) a rule like `h1, h2 { letter-spacing: -0.015em }`

stylesheet in source order wins — and the a11y sheet is injected after the
main one. Covers the correct fix: raise specificity to `body h1` AND compose
with the a11y variable via calc() so the user's accessibility control keeps
working instead of being hard-overridden.

availableCommands.name: git-stash-pop-theirs-ours-reversed

availableCommands.name: vitest-run-flag-and-tty-watch
availableCommands.description:

availableCommands.name: postgres-major-version-variable-splits-from-mount
availableCommands.description:

while the volume mount path is hardcoded — a combination that loses a database
silently from Postgres 18 onward. Use when: (1) a compose file contains
`postgres:${POSTGRES_VERSION:-17}`, `postgres:${PG_VERSION}`, or any templated
postgres tag, (2) you are about to add a version knob for a database image,

mount does not cover. Fix: hardcode the major, or move both together.

availableCommands.name: chart-downsample-hides-rate-dips

availableCommands.name: prisma-7-generated-client-needs-esm-package
availableCommands.description:
Fix `ReferenceError: exports is not defined in ES module scope` thrown
from a Prisma 7 generated client at runtime. Use when:
(1) `node dist/index.js` (or any production-style start) crashes with
`ReferenceError: exports is not defined in ES module scope` whose stack
points at `<pkg>/dist/generated/prisma/client.js` around the line
`Object.defineProperty(exports, "__esModule", { value: true });`,
(2) `yarn build` / `tsc` succeeded with no errors — the failure is
load-time, not compile-time, (3) the generated `client.js` contains BOTH
`globalThis['__dirname'] = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`
AND CJS-style `Object.defineProperty(exports, ...)` / `require(...)` in
the same file, (4) `dev` works under `tsx` / `ts-node` (which patches
CJS↔ESM at runtime) but production `node` crashes, (5) the package
containing the schema has no `"type"` field in its `package.json`, or
has `"type": "commonjs"`. Root cause: Prisma 7's `prisma-client`
generator emits TypeScript that uses `import.meta.url` (ESM-only). With
`module: Node16`/`NodeNext` in tsconfig, tsc decides whether to emit
ESM or CJS based on the nearest `package.json`'s `"type"` field. With
no `"type"`, the default is CJS — so tsc emits `exports.foo = ...`
alongside the ESM `import.meta.url`. Node sees `import.meta` and loads
the file as ESM, then crashes when it hits `exports`. Fix: add
`"type": "module"` to the package containing the Prisma schema (and
every package that imports it), then rebuild.

availableCommands.name: agentlogs-commit-message-quote-splice
availableCommands.description:
Explains and works around the `agentlogs` Claude Code plugin corrupting git
commit messages by injecting its "🔮 View transcript: <host>/s/..." line
MID-SENTENCE instead of at the end (host is agentlogs.ai by default, or a
self-hosted instance). Use when: (1) a commit message body is
visibly broken with a transcript URL spliced into the middle of a sentence,
(2) the corruption looks intermittent — some commits fine, others mangled,
(3) `git log --format=%B` shows the marker immediately before a double-quoted
phrase, (4) you are about to amend/force-push to "fix" commit messages and want
to know whether it will just happen again, (5) `.git/hooks` is empty so it is
clearly not a git hook. Root cause: the injector's `-m` regex uses `([^"]*)`,
which stops at the FIRST double quote in the message body.

availableCommands.name: vitepress-feature-icon-svg-string-form
availableCommands.description:
Fix VitePress home-page feature icons that render nothing (no icon tile, no
error) when you set `features[].icon` to an object like `{ svg: '<svg…>' }`.
Use when: (1) custom inline-SVG feature icons silently don't appear on a
VitePress `layout: home` page, (2) emoji icons work but SVG doesn't, (3) you
followed a snippet using `icon: { svg }` and got blank tiles. Root cause:
VitePress 1.6.x VPFeature.vue routes OBJECT icons to VPImage (needs `src`);
only a STRING icon is injected via v-html. Fix: pass raw SVG markup as a plain
string.

availableCommands.name: sentry-ruby-6x-before-send-to-hash
availableCommands.description:
Fix sentry-ruby 6.x "undefined method 'to_hash' for an instance of Sentry::ErrorEvent"
error that breaks all event capturing. Use when: (1) Sentry stops capturing events after
upgrading to sentry-ruby 6.x, (2) logs show "undefined method 'to_hash' for
Sentry::ErrorEvent", (3) before_send callback calls event.to_hash to filter parameters.
Root cause: ErrorEvent#to_hash was removed in sentry-ruby 6.x. The manual
ActiveSupport::ParameterFilter in before_send is redundant because sentry-rails
automatically applies Rails filter_parameters.
